title.rendered: I switched between Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Apple Watch Ultra 3: Here’s the better buy

content.rendered:
Samsung has finally unveiled the latest addition to its Ultra lineup: the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2. After going through its specs, my first question was simple: Is it better than the Apple Watch Ultra 3?

Both watches promise flagship performance, advanced health tracking, rugged durability, and smarter AI-powered features. But specifications only tell part of the story.

Instead of relying solely on spec sheets and marketing claims, I switched between the Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Apple Watch Ultra 3 to see how they actually compare in everyday use. Surprisingly, the winner wasn’t as obvious as I expected.

If you’re trying to decide between these two flagship smartwatches, you’re in the right place. I’ll compare the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Apple Watch Ultra 3 across design, display, performance, health tracking, battery life, smart features, and value to help you decide which one is right for you.

Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 vs Apple Watch Ultra 3: Quick specs comparison

On paper, both watches look incredibly close, but real-world use tells a different story.

Design and comfort: Rugged outside, premium on the wrist

The Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Apple Watch Ultra 3 are built for adventure, but they take very different approaches to design.

Samsung refines its signature look with the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2, continuing the iconic cushion design in a noticeably thinner profile. I like how the display and bezel flow together into a single, seamless form and give a clean, premium appearance. Crafted from Grade 4 titanium, it weighs only 61.5 g, making it comfortable for all-day wear despite its rugged build.

Samsung has also redesigned the buttons, making them more tactile and intuitive. I can now locate the Quick Button quickly even with gloves on.

Apple sticks to its instantly recognizable Ultra design. The Apple Watch Ultra 3 features a Grade 5 titanium frame that weighs 61.6 g. While it’s slightly larger than Samsung’s offering, it remains well-balanced on the wrist. The rectangular display, Digital Crown, and customizable Action Button prioritize usability, especially when navigating apps or checking notifications.

Despite their nearly identical weights, the two watches wear differently. The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 offers a more classic watch experience with its circular appearance, whereas I personally favor the bolder, functional look of the Apple Watch Ultra 3.

My verdict: Pick the Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 for the timeless classic look. In case you need a bigger display and more user-friendly interactions on the screen, choose Apple Watch Ultra 3.

Display quality: Samsung wins on brightness, Apple wins on screen space

When I first started comparing the Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Apple Watch Ultra 3, I assumed the displays would be nearly identical. But once I got to use both, I saw some major differences.

The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 immediately impressed me with its 1.52-inch Super AMOLED display. With a peak brightness of 5,000 nits, it was incredibly easy to read outdoors. Combined with its 498 × 498 resolution, everything from watch faces to workout metrics looked sharp and vibrant.

The Apple Watch Ultra 3, meanwhile, offers a larger 1.98-inch Retina LTPO3 OLED display with 3,000 nits of peak brightness. While it’s not as bright as Samsung’s on paper, I rarely found visibility to be an issue.

What I noticed more was the extra screen space. Long texts, Apple Maps navigation, or even viewing fitness data became a lot easier on the larger rectangular display and wide-angle OLED panel. Both watches use sapphire crystal glass, so I never worried about scratches during everyday use.

My Verdict: If I spent most of my time outdoors, I would definitely opt for the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 as its display performs better in direct sunlight. But for everyday tasks, I liked the Apple Watch Ultra 3‘s larger screen better.

Performance and software: The real battle isn’t speed; it’s the ecosystem

In terms of performance, I expected a clear winner. Instead, what stood out was how both watches are already so fast that the hardware almost fades into the background.

The Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 runs Wear OS 7 with One UI Watch 9, powered by the Snapdragon SW6100 Wear Elite (3nm) chipset. It sports a penta-core CPU, which makes everything – from launching apps to switching between workouts – very smooth. The best part is I can customize watch faces, widgets, and quick settings more freely.

Samsung blends Google’s ecosystem with Samsung-exclusive features. That means you get native access to Google Maps, Google Wallet, Gmail, Google Calendar, and more. Moreover, Samsung Galaxy phone owners gain even deeper integration through Galaxy AI features, SmartThings controls, camera remote functions, and seamless device switching.

The Apple Watch Ultra 3 runs watchOS 26 (upgradable to watchOS 27) and is powered by Apple’s S10 chip with a dual-core CPU and PowerVR GPU. Animations are buttery smooth, apps open instantly, and navigating the interface feels effortless.

I prefer it thanks to its seamless integrations with the iPhone, which makes activities such as sending messages, locating the phone, unlocking the Mac, controlling my smart home, or even making payments using Apple Pay seem almost effortless.

My Verdict: If you’re an Android user, the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 offers more customization and tight integration with Google’s ecosystem. As I am an iPhone user, Apple wins on software refinement and ecosystem integration.

Health and fitness tracking: Samsung packs in more features, Apple keeps it simple

Both Apple and Samsung have transformed their watches from simple notification devices into sophisticated health companions capable of tracking everything from heart rate and sleep to GPS workouts and recovery metrics.

The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is now equipped with AI health and fitness features intended to give us better personalized insights. The new Heart Health Score lets me get a simplified view of cardiovascular wellness, and Daily Cardio Load helps balance training and recovery. Fitness Index provides a broader view of physical fitness and supports personalized goals.

For outdoor athletes, Trail Run tracks elevation, climbing and terrain, while Nutrition Alert provides hydration guidance based on estimated sweat loss. The Ultra2 also introduces enhanced diving capabilities, tracking depth, dive time and water temperature, with an upcoming Mares-developed diving app adding more advanced metrics.

The Apple Watch Ultra 3 also stands out with advanced health monitoring and training tools. Its Hypertension Notifications can identify potential signs of chronic high blood pressure, while Sleep Score and sleep-apnea monitoring provide deeper insights into sleep quality and breathing disturbances.

For fitness, Ultra 3 offers Training Load, personalized Heart Rate Zones, Workout Buddy, and more. It also supports Power Zones for cycling, automatic swim-stroke detection, and multisport workout tracking. For adventurers, its full dive computer, Backtrack and built-in satellite communications add capabilities beyond conventional smartwatch fitness tracking.

My verdict: Choose Galaxy Watch Ultra2 for broader AI-powered health guidance, recovery and adventure features, whereas Apple Watch Ultra 3 is better for deeper workout analytics and a more established fitness ecosystem.

Battery life: Both keep up with you

If you want a smartwatch that can comfortably last through your day without constantly thinking about charging, the Galaxy Watch Ultra2 is the better fit.

Its 800mAh battery offers up to 60 hours with Always-On Display enabled. I went through long workouts, outdoor activities and overnight health tracking easily. Moreover, Samsung has included First Charging for the first time in a Galaxy Watch, providing up to 40% battery in just 30 minutes.

The Apple Watch Ultra 3 offers up to 42 hours of normal use and up to 72 hours in Low Power Mode. Its biggest advantage is charging speed, reaching up to 80% in around 45 minutes. I only charge for 15 minutes to get 12 hours of normal use.

Apple has claimed that the Watch Ultra 3 can go up to 14 hours of outdoor workout with full GPS and heart rate readings and up to 35 hours of outdoor workout with cellular in Low Power Mode with fewer GPS and heart rate readings.

My verdict: For longer, less interrupted use, I’d pick the Galaxy Watch Ultra2. If you value fast charging and flexible Low Power Mode, the Apple Watch Ultra 3 is more convenient.

Smart features and AI capabilities: Beyond fitness tracking

When choosing between the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Apple Watch Ultra 3, my deciding factor came down to which one fits my daily routine.

Both watches allow me to make phone calls and send messages, pay for goods, stream music, navigate, get calendar notifications and weather alerts, and install third-party apps. The real difference is in ecosystem integration and AI assistant.

The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is the more flexible pick for Android users, particularly if you want AI to feel like a natural part of the watch. I only need to raise my wrist to activate Google Gemini to ask questions, set reminders, control tasks and get help without a wake word or button click. It also brings Google Play Store to explore countless apps for productivity.


Given that I’m an iPhone user, the Apple Watch Ultra 3 feels like a natural part of my phone’s experience. Features such as Apple Pay, Find My, Continuity features, Siri, and tight integration with Apple services create a seamless experience. Moreover, Apple Intelligence features like Workout Buddy and Live Translation make it more practical.

My verdict: Choose the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 if you want conversational Gemini AI and the Google ecosystem. Go for the Apple Watch Ultra 3 if you already have an iPhone and want deeper ecosystem integration with personalized AI-powered fitness features.

Price & value: Which watch gives you more for your money?

The Galaxy Watch Ultra2 is the better value on price alone. Samsung lists it at $699.99, while the Apple Watch Ultra 3 starts at $799, putting the Galaxy ahead by $100.

That $100 difference matters if you have a Galaxy phone and want flagship features without stretching your budget. The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 packs a titanium design, LTE, a 5,000-nit display, an 800mAh battery and up to 60 hours of usage with always-on display enabled.

The Apple Watch Ultra 3 justifies its higher price with features that will appeal particularly to iPhone users, including 5G, satellite connectivity, a titanium case, up to 42 hours of normal battery life and deeper integration with the Apple ecosystem.

Our pick for value: Galaxy Watch Ultra2. It gives switchers more hardware and battery for less money. But if you’re moving to an iPhone, the extra $100 for the Apple Watch Ultra 3 can be worthwhile because its biggest advantage is how seamlessly it works with the rest of Apple’s ecosystem.

Who should buy the Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2?

Choose the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 if you:

  • Use a Samsung Galaxy smartphone
  • Prefer Android and Google services
  • Want a traditional round watch design
  • Value customization
  • Want excellent battery life
  • Enjoy Samsung Health and body composition tracking

Who should buy the Apple Watch Ultra 3?

Choose the Apple Watch Ultra 3 if you:

  • Own an iPhone
  • Want the smoothest smartwatch experience available
  • Depend on Apple Health and Apple’s ecosystem
  • Prefer a large rectangular display for apps and notifications
  • Want Ultra Wideband support for Precision Finding
  • Require Satellite connectivity, especially Emergency SOS via satellite

Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 vs Apple Watch Ultra 3: Which premium smartwatch should you buy?

After comparing design, display, software, health tracking, battery life, and overall value, one conclusion stands out: There isn’t a single winner. There are two winners, each dominating its own ecosystem.

If you’re an iPhone user like me, the Apple Watch Ultra 3 is the obvious choice. It offers seamless integration, polished software, and an ecosystem that feels cohesive from your wrist to your phone. Pairing with the right accessories, this is my adventure companion.

On the other hand, if you’re an Android user, especially someone with a Samsung Galaxy device, the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is the smartwatch I’d recommend without hesitation. It combines rugged hardware, excellent battery life, deep Google integration, and meaningful health features into a package that feels purpose-built for Android.

The biggest mistake you can make is choosing a smartwatch based solely on a feature comparison chart. In daily use, the experience is shaped far more by how well the watch fits into your existing ecosystem.

title.rendered: WhatsApp is moving parental controls into the iPhone settings screen

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is adding a dedicated parental controls entry to its iOS settings, so parents can start a parent-managed account without digging for the option. WABetaInfo spotted the section in WhatsApp for iOS 26.30.77 on the App Store, and it is reaching accounts in stages rather than all at once.

Tapping it opens a guided setup instead of a settings list. The parent needs both phones in hand: they scan a QR code or accept an invite, then finish the rest on the child’s phone and enter the child’s date of birth. WhatsApp keeps that date private and uses it internally. According to the report, the controls come off on their own once the child turns 18, and the features that were held back unlock then.

The controls themselves are not new

WhatsApp launched parent-managed accounts on March 11, 2026, for pre-teens. The account is limited to messaging and calling, so Channels, Status, Meta AI, and disappearing messages in one-to-one chats are all off the table.

Parents decide who can contact the account and which groups it can join. Messages from unknown numbers go into a separate Requests inbox for the parent to approve or ignore, and the whole panel sits behind a parent PIN on the managed device.

None of that means reading the child’s chats. Messages on a managed account stay end-to-end encrypted, and what the parent sees is account-level activity: new contacts, blocks and reports, privacy setting changes, and group invites.

Android got the same treatment first

The Android app picked up a parental controls entry in its settings screen in late July. The reason WhatsApp is bothering with an entry point at all is adoption. The feature shipped in March, but parents had to already know it existed to find it, and plenty never did.

Putting it in Settings is a low-effort fix for that, and it lines the two apps up so a household with an iPhone and an Android phone follows the same instructions.

What to check on your iPhone

Update WhatsApp from the App Store first, then open Settings in the app and look for the parental controls entry. If it is not there yet, the rollout has not reached your account, and WhatsApp says it should widen over the coming weeks. Parent-managed accounts are also still rolling out by region, so the account type may not be live where you are.

The setup runs on the child’s phone as much as your own, so it is worth having both charged and unlocked before you start. Setting up a parent-managed WhatsApp account then comes down to approving contacts, handling group invites, and locking the privacy settings behind the PIN.

App-level controls like this are also filling gaps that Screen Time never covered, which is the same direction Apple is heading with iOS 27’s child safety changes.

title.rendered: How to get Ironmouse Sprite in Fortnite

content.rendered:
After Hoshimachi Suisei got its own Fortnite cosmetics, Ironmouse is the next virtual internet celebrity to arrive in the highly popular online game. However, unlike the former, the latter has joined Fortnite’s growing sprite catalog, with the inclusion of the Ironmouse Sprite.

There is a good reason why players are rushing to grab hold of the Ironmouse Sprite at the moment. And that is because of its ability, which could be the difference between survival and elimination in the fiercely competitive moments of a match. The sprite allows players to regenerate their health when it is low and also offers a cloak during that recovery time.

Below, you can check out the various locations in Fortnite that other players are known to have found Ironmouse Sprite in. The guide also mentions other ways of obtaining the sought-after sprite, besides chest-hunting.

Where to find Ironmouse Sprite in Fortnite

Hunting for chests and vaults

As a Mythic-tier item, Ironmouse Sprite is one of the rarer sprites in Fortnite. As a result, it is unlikely to be spotted out in the open and has a higher chance of being found via chests. In particular, special chest variants, such as the Sprite Chest, should be your primary target for finding the Ironmouse Sprite as soon as possible. For additional help in revealing Sprite Chest locations, you can also use the Sprite Locator item, which can be found during a Battle Royale match.

Apart from chests, you can also find this elusive sprite in hidden vaults, which are often situated underground. Importantly, these vaults can only be unlocked with a key, so it is advisable to scour the nearby neighborhoods for one when you come across a vault door.

Taking it from an enemy

If you want to skip the chest hunt and are feeling opportunistic, you can simply take the Ironmouse Sprite from your opponent during a match. Before you board the Battle Bus, take a look at the backs of all other players in the lobby. If you spot your desired sprite, try to remember the appearance of the player.

Once the Battle Bus is airborne, keep an eye out for that same player and time your jump with him. Follow the player to his landing zone, pursue, and then eliminate him to pick up the Ironmouse Sprite as the loot.

Indexing it from a friend

The official Fortnite Discord is a thriving online community, and there is a specific channel where you could find help in completing your sprite collection. You just have to go to the “sprite-runners-network” channel and request someone who already has the Ironmouse Sprite to share.

How this works is that you both join the same match, and then you accept the offered sprite and extract it to index it. Once that part is over, you can return the sprite to its original owner in the next match, following the same process. After this, in the Sprites tab, you will be able to restore the Ironmouse Sprite to your collection by using Sprite Dust.

Final note

Thanks to the introduction of the Ironmouse Sprite, Fortnite players have a chance to add another powerful Sprite to their inventory. In the past, Boss Sprite and Demon Sprite have provided players with decisive health boosts, and now the virtual streamer-inspired Sprite has stepped into a similar role. With more variants continuing to join the game, players looking to keep track of all Sprites in Fortnite will have another addition to their collection to discover.

Over the course of the next few weeks, it will be interesting to see how widespread the Ironmouse Sprite becomes as more players get their hands on it. Moreover, another thing worth keeping track of is how popular it stays once newer Sprites are rolled out in the Epic Games-developed title.

  • How to get Batman Sprite in Fortnite

title.rendered: iPhone 17 prices may rise today, a month before the iPhone 18 Pro arrives

content.rendered:
Apple may raise iPhone 17 prices on August 10, according to a Weibo post from supply-chain leaker Fixed Focus Digital. That date is today. Apple has announced nothing, and the U.S. store still shows launch pricing as this is written.

The leaker did not sound confident. He described it as a rumor going around rather than something he had confirmed, and the date is the only specific detail in the post. There are no figures, no model list, and no regions. The same post claimed Apple has pulled back on a planned production increase for some lines, though the reported numbers vary between outlets and that detail is just as thin.

What the iPhone 17 costs right now

Apple’s U.S. store lists the same starting prices the lineup launched with in September 2025:

Apple charges $30 more for an iPhone 17 bought without carrier activation, so the unlocked 256GB model sits at $829 today.

Memory costs are the reason this rumor is credible at all

A mid-cycle price increase on a phone already sitting on shelves is unusual for Apple. The company normally holds a price for the full year and resets it at the next launch. This year, memory is breaking that pattern.

On Apple’s Q3 earnings call on July 30, Tim Cook said Apple “reluctantly raised prices” because “we’re in, what I would characterize as a hundred-year flood on the memory pricing with exponential increases in memory prices.” He added that Apple expects to pay even more for memory in the September quarter than it did in June.

That flood has already hit everything except the phone. Apple raised prices on Macs, iPads, Vision Pro, Apple TV, and HomePod in late June, with the Mac Studio jumping by as much as $1,300. iPhone, Apple Watch, AirPods, and Studio Display were left untouched.

One iPhone exception already exists. Apple raised Japanese iPhone prices on July 17, pushing the iPhone 17 in Japan from ¥129,800 to ¥142,800, close to a 10% jump, with iPhone Air rising 11.3%. A weak yen carried most of that, but it showed Apple is willing to reprice a current iPhone mid-cycle.

Why moving now, rather than in September, would make sense

The iPhone 17 is not about to disappear. Apple is expected to launch the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the foldable iPhone in September, while the standard iPhone 18 slips to spring 2027. That leaves the iPhone 17 and iPhone Air as Apple’s mainstream phones for another six months or so.

Repricing them now also softens what comes next. Apple had reportedly been working to keep iPhone 18 Pro prices level with the iPhone 17 Pro, negotiating hard with Samsung and SK Hynix to protect that $1,099 starting point. If those talks did not land, a jump from $1,099 straight to a higher iPhone 18 Pro number lands harder than two smaller steps.

None of that is evidence the increase is happening today. It only explains why the rumor is not absurd. Fixed Focus Digital’s record is mixed, the post carries no numbers, and Apple has said nothing. If you were planning to buy an iPhone 17 this month, the practical move is to check the price before you order, not to panic-buy on a Weibo post.

title.rendered: Foldable iPhone Ultra’s launch colors may be silver and dark blue

content.rendered:
Leaker Sonny Dickson has posted photos of two camera protectors made for Apple’s foldable iPhone, one in silver and one in a very dark blue. He says the pair reflects two of the colors planned for the device.

These are third-party accessories built from supply-chain information, not Apple parts, so treat the finishes as a close match rather than an exact one. Dickson’s accessory and dummy-unit leaks have mostly held up, including his early look at this year’s iPhone 18 Pro colors. The blue here is dark enough to pass for black across a room, in the same territory as iPhone 17 Pro’s Deep Blue.

The protectors wrap the camera plateau, so they also trace its shape: two lenses side by side, a pill-shaped flash, and a LiDAR scanner. That lines up with the dummy units that have been circulating since spring.

Dark blue replaces the white everyone expected

Apple’s foldable has been tied to a short color list since spring. A Macworld supply-chain source described a palette of silver, white, and an indigo shade close to iPhone 17 Pro’s Deep Blue, and Weibo leaker Instant Digital said the phone would ship in two finishes. In June, an image of an alleged white unit spread as the first “confirmed” color.

Dickson’s protectors point somewhere else. Silver survives, but the second color is blue rather than white, or the dark gray floated in February.

Two colors fits a first-generation foldable

iPhone 18 Pro is expected in four finishes this year. A two-color launch is what a new, supply-constrained product usually gets: fewer variants to build, fewer yield problems, and less stock sitting unsold at a price expected to start near $2,000.

When you could actually buy one

Apple has not announced its September event yet. The foldable is expected to be introduced next month alongside iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, though Ming-Chi Kuo expects a gap between the announcement and pre-orders, the way the iPhone X was shown in September 2017 and only went on sale at the end of October. That leaves about a month for the color list to shift again, and Apple has changed finishes late before.

title.rendered: Ceramic could return to the Apple Watch with Series 12

content.rendered:
Apple is planning to bring the ceramic Apple Watch case back, according to Mark Gurman’s Power On newsletter. He says the company is plotting the return of a ceramic option either this year or next, which puts it in play for the Series 12 in September or the 2027 model. Gurman did not narrow it down further, so a ceramic Series 12 is possible rather than planned.

What else is expected this year

The ceramic case is one part of a fairly small update. Gurman says this year’s watches will add new color and band options along with health and fitness improvements, and the headline internal change is a new chip, the first meaningful speed bump since the Series 10. He has also said Apple is testing only three watches for 2026, the Series 12 in Wi-Fi and cellular versions plus the Apple Watch Ultra 4, with no new SE.

Ceramic has come and gone twice already

Apple has never kept ceramic in the lineup for long. It arrived as the top-tier Edition finish, disappeared, came back, and then vanished again.

The material itself was compressed zirconia and alumina powder polished with a diamond slurry, which Apple said made it four times as hard as stainless steel. Six years after it was dropped, the white ceramic Series 5 is still one of the more sought-after Apple Watches on the resale market.

The price is the real question

Ceramic was always the most expensive Apple Watch, and nothing about the process has gotten cheaper. For context, the current lineup starts at $399 for an aluminum Series 11, $699 for titanium, and $799 for the Ultra 3. The last ceramic model cost $1,299.

No pricing has leaked for a ceramic Series 12. What is clear is that this would be a finish for people who want a more expensive watch, not a feature upgrade for everyone else.

A bigger rethink is happening behind it

Gurman also reports that Apple’s industrial design team has spent the past year reconsidering what a smartwatch should be, in response to smart rings and screenless fitness bands. Ideas under discussion include a round display, a tracker with no screen at all, cheaper models below the SE, and premium tiers above the Ultra and Hermès versions. Apple has not settled on a direction, and Gurman called a round watch unlikely to ship.

That makes ceramic a stopgap of sorts. Until Apple decides what the next Apple Watch actually looks like, new materials and colors are the easiest way to make an unchanged design feel new.

Series 12 and Ultra 4 are expected at Apple’s September event, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro models and the first foldable iPhone. If ceramic misses that date, 2027 is the next window.

title.rendered: What is My Eyes Only in Snapchat and how I use it to keep private Snaps safe

content.rendered:
The first time I handed my phone to a friend to show a funny Snapchat memory, I realized that not every photo in my Memories was meant for everyone to see. There were personal screenshots, family pictures, and a few photos I simply wanted to keep private.

That’s when I discovered My Eyes Only in Snapchat. Honestly, it’s one of those features I wish I’d started using much earlier. It adds an extra layer of privacy without making your photos difficult to access.

In this guide, I’ll explain what My Eyes Only is on Snapchat, how I use it, how to set it up, and the mistakes I almost made so you don’t have to repeat them.

What is My Eyes Only on Snapchat?

My Eyes Only is a private section inside Snapchat Memories where you can store your Snaps and Stories from your Memories behind a separate 4-digit passcode or alphanumeric passphrase.

Unlike regular Memories, the content stored here cannot be viewed unless someone enters your My Eyes Only passcode. Even if another person is holding your unlocked phone, they still can’t open your hidden Snaps without that code.

When I first discovered it, I immediately moved all my private memories and personal photos and videos from my Camera Roll to My Eyes Only. It seems like creating a private photo vault without downloading any other apps.

It is particularly useful when you:

  • Frequently hand your phone to friends or family
  • Save personal photos in Snapchat
  • Want an extra privacy layer
  • Keep screenshots you don’t want others scrolling through

Simply put, regular Memories are for everyday photos I don’t mind opening quickly. My Eyes Only is Snapchat’s built-in secure folder where anything personal stays.

Why I prefer using My Eyes Only

Many people think this feature is only for hiding embarrassing photos. I completely disagree. For me, it’s about privacy, not secrecy.

These are the main reasons for using it.

  • It gives me peace of mind: I often hand my phone to someone to show vacation photos or funny videos. Before using My Eyes Only, I was always worried someone would accidentally swipe one photo too far. Now I don’t think about it.
  • Keeps my Memories organized: I don’t want screenshots, IDs, notes, or personal pictures mixed with travel memories and funny Snaps. Separating them actually makes Memories cleaner.
  • Feels like having a private album: Instead of downloading another vault app, Snapchat already gives me one that’s built into the app. Less clutter, less hassle.
  • Protects sensitive content: Whether it’s financial screenshots, important documents, or personal moments, I know they’re hidden behind another layer of security. That’s enough for my everyday use.

How to set up My Eyes Only in Snapchat

Setting it up only takes a minute.

Here’s exactly how I did it.

  1. Open Snapchat.
  2. Swipe up from the camera interface to open Memories.
  3. Go to the My Eyes Only tab.
  4. Choose Set Up, then tap Quick Setup.
  5. Create a 4-digit passcode. Choose one you’ll actually remember. For a stronger password, select Use Passphrase at the bottom and create one.
  6. Now, re-enter your passcode to confirm.
  7. Read Snapchat’s warning carefully and agree to it. This is important.
  8. Tap Continue > Finish to complete the setup. Your private vault is now ready.

How I move photos and videos to My Eyes Only

Once everything was set up, moving my private content took only a few seconds.

Here’s how.

  1. Open Memories.
  2. Press and hold a Snap and select as many as you want. You may also choose photos and videos from Stories and Recents from the Camera Roll section.
  3. Now, tap the three-dot icon at the bottom left corner.
  4. Choose Move to My Eyes Only.
  5. Tap Move to confirm the action. Enter your passcode if prompted.

That’s it.

The selected Snap disappears from your regular Memories and moves into the protected folder. If you move media from your Camera Roll, Snapchat will prompt you to delete the original from there for extra privacy.

Note: You can only store Camera Roll videos shorter than 10 seconds in My Eyes Only.

Save Snaps to My Eyes Only by default

One feature I appreciate is the option to save new private Snaps directly to My Eyes Only instead of first saving them in regular Memories on iOS.

If you already know certain content should remain private, saving it directly into My Eyes Only saves time and avoids forgetting to move it later. I mainly use this for personal screenshots and sensitive images.

  1. Launch Snapchat and tap your Bitmoji at the top to access your profile.
  2. Select the gear icon to open Settings.
  3. Scroll down and tap Memories.
  4. Toggle on Save to My Eyes Only by Default.

How to view Snaps and remove them from My Eyes Only

Viewing hidden Snaps is simple.

  1. Open Snapchat and swipe up for Memories.
  2. Move to the My Eyes Only section.
  3. Enter your passcode.


Everything appears exactly as you saved it. From here, you can edit, remix, export, and share the Snaps.

If I ever want to move something back:

  1. Press and hold the Snap.
  2. Tap the three-dot icon and select Unhide Snap.
  3. It returns to regular Memories.
  4. Otherwise, you may select Delete Snap to remove it permanently.

The process feels surprisingly smooth. You may even select multiple Snaps together to unhide them quickly.

How to change your My Eyes Only passcode

There may come an instance when you accidentally reveal your My Eyes Only passcode to someone. However, considering the privacy of the contents, you won’t want anyone to access it using the said passcode. In that case, you can quickly change your Snapchat My Eyes Only passcode.

Here’s how.

  1. Open Memories and go to My Eyes Only.
  2. On the passcode page, tap Options at the bottom right.
  3. Choose Change Passcode.
  4. Now, enter your current passcode and create a new one.
  5. Choose a new 4-digit passcode and re-enter it to confirm.
  6. Agree to the terms and conditions, then tap Continue.
  7. Finally, tap Finish.

I only recommend changing it when necessary because you’ll need to remember the new passcode immediately.

What happens if you forget your My Eyes Only passcode?

This is the one lesson I wish someone had told me sooner: Snapchat cannot recover your hidden Snaps if you forget your passcode.

Yes, you can reset the passcode. But resetting it erases everything stored inside My Eyes Only. That’s not a bug. It’s how Snapchat protects your privacy. That’s why I saved my passcode in my password manager because I never want to lose access to those memories.

Here’s how you can reset your My Eyes Only passcode if you forget it:

  1. Head to the My Eyes Only section on the Snapchat app.
  2. Here, tap on Options at the bottom right.
  3. Next, tap the Forgot Passcode button, then enter your Snapchat Account password.
  4. Agree to the terms and conditions and tap on Continue.
  5. Now, choose a new 4-digit passcode and reenter it to confirm.
  6. Again, agree to the terms and conditions and tap on Continue.
  7. Tap Finish.

Your My Eyes Only folder will open as if you set it now.

A few things I wish I knew before using it

After using My Eyes Only for quite a while, here are the things that surprised me.

  • Privacy Doesn’t Mean Backup: If a memory is truly important, don’t rely only on Snapchat. Always keep another backup.
  • Organize Early: Moving hundreds of Snaps later becomes tedious. It’s easier to organize as you go or enable moving to My Eyes Only as default.
  • Use It for Privacy Only: Not every photo belongs in My Eyes Only. I only store content I’d genuinely be uncomfortable showing someone if they borrowed my phone. That keeps the folder manageable.

Common My Eyes Only problems and fixes

Keep your private Snaps secure!

After using My Eyes Only a few times, I genuinely recommend it to almost every Snapchat user. It gives control over who sees my personal memories.

If you regularly save screenshots, personal photos, or anything you’d rather keep away from curious eyes, turning on My Eyes Only takes less than five minutes and can save you from some awkward moments later. However, it would be nice if Snapchat added a way to recover the forgotten passcode for users who wish to stick to the original passcode.

What do you think about this feature? Let me know in the comments below!

@graph.name: How to Set Up My Eyes Only on Snapchat from iPhone
@graph.description: Secure your private snaps on Snapchat by setting up the My Eyes Only feature with a 4-digit passcode on your iPhone.

step.name: Access Memories section
step.text: Open the Snapchat app and swipe up on the Camera tab to access the Memories section. Swipe right on the horizontal menu bar below the Search bar and tap My Eyes Only.

itemListElement.text: Swipe up on the Camera tab.
Swipe right in the menu bar and tap My Eyes Only.

step.name: Start setup
step.text: Tap the Set Up button, then tap Quick Setup to begin configuring My Eyes Only.

step.name: Set a passcode
step.text: Choose a 4-digit passcode, then reenter it to confirm your choice.

step.name: Agree to terms
step.text: Review the terms and conditions, tap the checkbox to agree, then tap Continue to finish setup.

@graph.name: How to Add Snaps to My Eyes Only
@graph.description: Hide selected snaps in Snapchat by moving them to My Eyes Only for added privacy.

tool.name: iPhone or Android phone with Snapchat app

step.name: Open Memories section
step.text: In the Snapchat app, swipe up on the default Camera tab to open the Memories section.

itemListElement.text: Swipe up on the Camera tab.

step.name: Select snap
step.text: Long press on the snap you want to hide, then tap the Three Dot button that appears at the bottom.

itemListElement.text: Long press on the desired snap.

step.name: Hide snap in My Eyes Only
step.text: From the pop-up menu, tap Hide Snap (My Eyes Only).

step.name: Confirm move
step.text: Tap the Move button in the confirmation prompt to send the snap to My Eyes Only.

step.name: Access My Eyes Only options

step.name: Access My Eyes Only options

step.name: Access Snapchat profile

step.name: Open Snapchat settings
step.text: Tap the Settings icon at the top right corner of your profile screen.

step.name: Navigate to Memories settings

step.name: Enable saving to My Eyes Only

keyPoints.title: Introduction to Snapchat's My Eyes Only Feature
keyPoints.explanation: My Eyes Only is a password-protected folder within Snapchat Memories that allows users to securely store private snaps separate from their main gallery.

keyPoints.title: Setting Up My Eyes Only on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Users can set up My Eyes Only by accessing Memories, selecting the option to create a 4-digit passcode, and completing the setup process through the Snapchat app.

keyPoints.title: Adding Snaps to My Eyes Only
keyPoints.explanation: Snaps can be moved to My Eyes Only by selecting them in Memories, tapping the options menu, and choosing 'Hide Snap' to secure them behind the passcode.

keyPoints.title: Changing and Resetting the My Eyes Only Password
keyPoints.explanation: Users can change their passcode from the options within My Eyes Only or reset it using their Snapchat account password if they forget the current passcode.

keyPoints.title: Default Saving to My Eyes Only
keyPoints.explanation: Snapchat offers an option to automatically save all new snaps directly to My Eyes Only, enhancing privacy without manual moving of individual snaps.

title.rendered: Fortnite brings back X-Men skins: Here’s how to get them

content.rendered:
X-Men skins modeled around Cyclops, Gambit, Rogue, Colossus, and Jubilee, have made their way into Fortnite. It marks the return of these superhero skins in the game after a span of nearly four months.

Initially added between 2022 and 2024, these X-Men skins have been a regular part of the Item Shop ever since then. The current run will ensure these items are up for grabs until August 10, 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET. While the Cyclops and Colossus outfits are selling for 2,000 V-Bucks, other X-Men skins are priced at 1,500 V-Bucks. You can go through the steps below to claim the desired one from the lot.

Steps to claim X-Men skins in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, go to the Shop tab.
  2. Then, scroll down to the X-Men section and select your desired character skin.
  3. At last, press and hold the Purchase button to confirm your decision.

For those who want to own the Rogue and Gambit skins, there is also an option to purchase the namesake bundle worth 2,100 V-Bucks, which also comes with some extra in-game goodies. On the other hand, Cyclops, Colossus, and Jubilee have their own bundle titled X-Men Bundle. It also contains relevant bonus items and is priced at 3,800 V-Bucks.

All X-Men cosmetics in Fortnite

1. Kinetic Cards (back bling)

Available with: Gambit skin, Rogue & Gambit Bundle

2. Suit Surfer (glider)

Price: 800 V-Bucks

3. Xavier’s School For Gifted Youngsters (back bling)

Available with: Rogue skin, Rogue & Gambit Bundle

4. Hands Off! (emote)

Price: 300 V-Bucks
Available with: Rogue skin, Rogue & Gambit Bundle

5. Rogue & Gambit (loading screen)

Exclusively available with: Rogue & Gambit Bundle

6. Holo X-Axe (pickaxe)

Price: 500 V-Bucks

7. The Blackbird (glider)

Price: 800 V-Bucks

8. X-Pack (back bling)

Available with: Cyclops skin, X-Men Bundle

9. Op-Pick-tal Blast Axe (pickaxe)

Available with: Cyclops skin, X-Men Bundle

10. Optic Blast! (emote)

Available with: Cyclops skin, X-Men Bundle

11. Cyclops Flair (wrap)

Exclusively available with: X-Men Bundle

12. Osmium Shield (back bling)

Available with: Colossus skin, X-Men Bundle

13. Colossal Hammer (pickaxe)

Available with: Colossus skin, X-Men Bundle

14. Sentinel Squats (emote)

Available with: Colossus skin, X-Men Bundle

15. Lumikinetic Bat (pickaxe)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: X-Men Bundle

16. Jubilee’s Blades (back bling)

Available with: Jubilee skin, X-Men Bundle

Wrapping up

While X-Men cosmetics are currently leading the charge for Marvel in the Item Shop, a wide variety of the comic publisher’s superheroes and supervillains have previously also made the cut, to say the least. From Spider-Man Brand New Day Fortnite skins to entire Marvel-themed seasons, their fans have had plenty to enjoy in the game over the years.

Given how Marvel has been a longtime major collaborator for Epic’s multiplayer title, it is reasonable to expect that the cascade of in-game items will continue for the foreseeable future. With that in mind, Avengers Doomsday, MCU’s next big superhero team-up flick, emerges as a prime candidate for the next notable Fortnite-Marvel partnership. However, what all new content that potential collab brings is something only time will tell.

FAQs

In which season were these X-Men skins first rolled out in Fortnite?

They were first released in Chapter 5 Season 3, which took place from May 2024 to August 2024.

Are all X-Men members part of the ongoing promotion in Fortnite?

No, certain key X-Men, such as Professor X, Storm, and Wolverine, are missing.

Which other superhero teams have previously appeared in Fortnite?

Superhero teams that have had their cosmetics show up in the Shop are Avengers, Fantastic Four, and Guardians Of The Galaxy, among others.

title.rendered: Jujutsu Shenanigans codes (August 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Jujutsu Shenanigans codes on August 07, 2026

Jujutsu Shenanigans puts you in a destructible arena where timing and character knowledge matter more than anything a code can buy. Still, developer codes are worth redeeming because they unlock cash, achievements, and limited emotes that may not return once they expire.

The current reward is the Woven Insight emote and Nep Achievement. Its code is a 17-character mix of letters and numbers, so copy it exactly and claim it before jumping into a fight. It will not improve your combos or awakening meter, but it gives you a collectible that normal wins cannot unlock.

All working Jujutsu Shenanigans codes

  • A7D2L26RNEPG74A3Q: (New) Nep Achievement and Woven Insight emote

Expired Jujutsu Shenanigans codes

SLATECONCRETE, RIPBOWE, X6X31F47UN8JM1NEP, 67, WHYEMOTEDISSAPEAR, JJS1YEAR, WHYISTHISCODEHIDDEN, 370MVISITS, 120MVISITS, 20MVISITS

These older codes are listed as inactive by the game’s community code ledger. A few trackers still recycle some of them as working, but they are not worth trying before the active code above.

Jujutsu Shenanigans codes can be unusually short-lived. Several cash codes lasted only a few days, while X6X31F47UN8JM1NEP stopped after the first 100 redemptions.

How to redeem Jujutsu Shenanigans codes

You can use a code as soon as you enter the game; there is no listed level or tutorial requirement.

  1. Open Jujutsu Shenanigans on Roblox.
  2. Click the Shop icon at the top-left of the screen.
  3. Open the Rewards tab.
  4. Paste the working code into the text box.
  5. Select Redeem or press Enter to claim it.

Check your emotes after redemption. The current code also adds the Nep Achievement to your account.

Why your Jujutsu Shenanigans code is not working

The active code is a 17-character mix of letters and numbers, so a small typing mistake is the most likely problem. Check these before giving up:

  • You mistyped a letter or number, changed the capitalization, or added a space.
  • The code expired after the list was updated.
  • You already redeemed it on your Roblox account.
  • The reward had a limited number of claims.
  • Your server has not picked up a new code yet.
  • Roblox or Jujutsu Shenanigans is having a temporary server issue.

Copy and paste the code wherever possible. If a newly released code fails, leave the game and join a fresh server before assuming it is dead.

Where to find more Jujutsu Shenanigans codes

New codes appear in the game’s Update Notes, which you can open through the Notebook icon. The developers sometimes announce only that a code exists and hide it somewhere on the map, so new drops can turn into a short scavenger hunt.

These are the most useful official and community pages to watch:

  • Jujutsu Shenanigans on Roblox
  • Tze’s Shenanigans Roblox community
  • the z’s Discord server

The Discord and in-game notes are the fastest sources, but older messages are easy to miss once another update lands. Bookmark this page if you want the working and expired codes kept separate.

If you want more free rewards, check out the latest Ninja Time codes, Dragon Soul codes, and our complete list of all Roblox game codes.

What is Jujutsu Shenanigans?

Jujutsu Shenanigans is a Roblox battlegrounds game by Tze’s Shenanigans. You fight other players with anime-inspired abilities, build an awakening meter, and smash through a destructible arena.

Codes mostly add cash, achievements, or emotes to that loop. They will not improve your combos, but an exclusive emote gives you one more way to celebrate after landing them.

title.rendered: Survive Zombie Arena codes (August 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Survive Zombie Arena codes on August 10, 2026

Survive Zombie Arena gives you little breathing room once the tougher zombie waves arrive. Credits help you unlock stronger guns and classes, while crate spins and shard boosts make it easier to improve your setup without repeating the same early grind.

The current code pool is especially useful because it covers several kinds of rewards. You can claim straight Credit payouts, Bloodmoon and Artifact spins, and timed multipliers for Credits or event shards. Save the timed boosts for a proper play session so you can get more value from them.

Copy every code exactly as shown, including the capital letters. Redeem the four newest update codes first, then work through the older Credit and event rewards before another patch removes them.

All working Survive Zombie Arena codes

  • patchboi: 2x arena credits for 4 hours (NEW)
  • TUNDRASZN: (NEW) 2x Bloodmoon Shards for 48 hours and 2x arena credits for 4 hours
  • BOSSRUSH: (NEW) 3,500 Credits and 2x Ultra Yeti encounter chance for 12 hours
  • DELAYSAHUR: (NEW) 4,500 Credits + 2 Bloodmoon Crate spins
  • UPDATE0.5: (NEW) 5,000 Credits, 2x Credits for 8 hours, and 2x Bloodmoon Shards for 12 hours
  • BEWARETHETUNDRA: 1 Artifact Crate Spin
  • LUVUGUYS: 1 Bloodmoon Spin
  • COOLPFPSWAG: 3 Bloodmoon Spins and 2x Bloodmoon Shards for 4 hours
  • DELAY: 2,500 Credits and 1 Bloodmoon Crate
  • UPDATEDAYSWAG: 1,069 Credits and 1 Bloodmoon Crate
  • GALACTIC: 2x Void Shards for 24 hours
  • Zombies: 2,500 Credits

Expired Survive Zombie Arena codes

SORRY4DELAY, MUTATE

These codes no longer work on current servers.

How to redeem Survive Zombie Arena codes

The code box sits inside the Shop menu while you are in the lobby. You do not need to join the developer’s Roblox group before using it.

  1. Open Survive Zombie Arena on Roblox.
  2. Click Shop on the left side of the lobby.
  3. Scroll to the Redeem Codes section.
  4. Paste a working code into the box.
  5. Click Redeem to claim the reward.

Why your code is not working

Most failures come from an expired code, a typing mistake, or a server that has not picked up the newest update.

  • The code has expired.
  • You changed a capital letter or added an extra space.
  • You already redeemed the code on your Roblox account.
  • You joined an older server running a previous game version.
  • Roblox or Survive Zombie Arena is having a temporary server issue.

Copy and paste the code instead of typing it. If a brand-new code still fails, leave the game, join a fresh server, and try once more before assuming it is dead.

Where to find more Survive Zombie Arena codes

New codes usually arrive with updates, events, delays, or shutdown fixes. These are the useful official places to watch:

  • Survive Zombie Arena Roblox page
  • Nectarforge Studios Roblox community
  • Survive Zombie Arena Discord server

The Discord is the fastest place to catch a drop, but old and expired codes can get buried in update chatter. Bookmark this page if you want a shorter list that separates working rewards from dead codes.

If you want more free rewards, check out the latest Jujutsu Shenanigans codes, Ninja Time codes, and our complete list of all Roblox game codes.

What is Survive Zombie Arena?

Survive Zombie Arena is a Roblox wave-survival shooter by Nectarforge Studios. You fight increasingly large zombie waves, unlock stronger guns, pick a class, team up with other players, and try to climb the wave leaderboard.

Codes cut part of the early resource grind, while the timed boosts help most when you can stay for a full run.

title.rendered: Fortnite Squid Game skins return: Here’s how to get them

content.rendered:
Squid Game has officially returned to the Fortnite Item Shop after more than three months away. Skins and other cosmetics inspired by the hugely popular Netflix series and its iconic challenges are once again available for a limited time.

Originally introduced in June 2025, the Squid Game collaboration has rotated in and out of the Fortnite Item Shop several times over the past year. After its previous appearance in March, the collection is finally back and will remain available until August 8 at 8 PM ET.

Individual Squid Game Participant outfits cost 1,200 V-Bucks each, while the Games Manager and Games Guard outfits are priced at 1,500 V-Bucks each. If you’re planning to add them to your locker, here’s how to get them before they leave the shop again.

How to get Squid Game skins in Fortnite

Buying the Squid Game cosmetics is straightforward.

  1. In Fortnite, go to the Shop tab
  2. Next, scroll down all the way until you reach the Squid Game section and then select your desired skin
  3. Finally, press and hold the Purchase button to confirm your decision.

If you’re planning to collect the entire collaboration, you can also buy the Squid Bundle for 3,000 V-Bucks. It includes all 12 outfits released as part of the crossover, making it the best-value option for players who want the complete set.

All Squid Game cosmetics available in Fortnite

Besides the character outfits, Epic Games has also brought back several themed cosmetics.

1. Ddakji Box (back bling)

Price: 300 V-Bucks
Also available in: Squid Accessories Bundle

2. Delicious Dalgona (back bling)

Price: 300 V-Bucks
Also available in: Squid Accessories Bundle

3. Lil’ Prized Piggy Bank (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available in: Squid Accessories Bundle

4. Squid Shapes (wrap)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available in: Squid Accessories Bundle

Players who want every accessory can purchase the Squid Accessories Bundle for 700 V-Bucks, which combines all four cosmetics at a discounted price.

Should you buy the Squid Game bundle?

If you’re only interested in one or two characters, purchasing them individually makes the most sense. However, players who want the complete Squid Game collection will save V-Bucks by picking up the Squid Bundle, which includes all 12 outfits in a single purchase.

Likewise, the Squid Accessories Bundle is the better value if you’re planning to collect every back bling, wrap, and emote instead of buying each cosmetic separately.

Since the collaboration is only available for a limited time, it’s worth deciding before the shop refreshes on August 8 at 8 PM ET.

Wrapping up

Thanks to the massive success of its first two seasons, Squid Game remains one of Netflix’s biggest global franchises. It’s also one of several high-profile Netflix Originals that have collaborated with Fortnite over the years, joining titles like Stranger Things, K-Pop Demon Hunters, and Arcane: League of Legends.

These collaborations continue to attract players from well beyond Fortnite’s traditional audience, giving fans another reason to jump into the game whenever a favorite franchise returns. As Epic Games keeps expanding its lineup of crossover events with major entertainment brands, Fortnite continues moving closer to the metaverse-style experience the company has envisioned for years.

In case you missed:

  • How to get the Lil Tecca skin in Fortnite
  • How to get Borderlands skins in Fortnite
  • How to get Spider-Man Brand New Day skins
  • How to get X-Men skins in Fortnite

mainEntity.name: Are all X-Men members part of the ongoing promotion in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, certain key X-Men, such as Professor X, Storm, and Wolverine, are missing.

mainEntity.name: Which other superhero teams have previously appeared in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Superhero teams that have had their cosmetics show up in the Shop are Avengers, Fantastic Four, and Guardians Of The Galaxy, among others.

title.rendered: Apple takes 65% of premium smartphone sales as high-end market hits record share

content.rendered:
Apple captured 65% of global premium smartphone unit sales in the first half of 2026, according to a new Counterpoint Research report. Counterpoint defines premium phones as models with a wholesale average selling price of at least $600.

The segment grew 5% year over year and reached a record 29% of all smartphone sales, up from 25% in H1 2025. Apple’s premium sales rose 9%, driven by the iPhone 17 series—especially the base iPhone 17.

Apple recovered some share, but China remains a pressure point

Apple’s 65% share is up from 63% in H1 2025, though it remains well below the 74% it held in H1 2022. Samsung stayed at 19%, giving the two companies a combined 84% of premium unit sales.

Counterpoint attributes Apple’s longer-term decline mainly to stronger competition in China, where Huawei, Xiaomi, OPPO, and vivo have expanded their flagship lineups. OPPO recorded the fastest growth in the premium segment at 69% year over year, while vivo grew 20%. The report did not disclose their individual market shares.

Higher component costs are pushing buyers upmarket

Counterpoint says rising memory and component costs are hitting low- and mid-range phones harder. As those devices become more expensive, the gap between a mid-range Android phone and an older or discounted flagship becomes smaller.

Premium brands can also absorb more of those costs through higher margins. The shift stands out against a weak broader market: Apple reached a record 20% global shipment share in Q2 even as total smartphone shipments fell 11% year over year, according to separate Counterpoint estimates.

Financing, trade-ins, and buyback plans are doing more of the work too. Apple recently launched its Apple Upgrade leasing program in the US, while Samsung has expanded its Galaxy Forever program to more markets.

Counterpoint expects Apple and Samsung to retain their premium-market lead, helped by their ecosystems, brand strength, and position in developed markets. In China, however, Huawei and Xiaomi are well placed to keep gaining ground as their premium lineups grow.

title.rendered: macOS Tahoe 26.6.1 fixes a high-severity Screen Sharing flaw

content.rendered:
Apple has released macOS Tahoe 26.6.1 to patch a Screen Sharing flaw that could let an attacker on the network authenticate without valid credentials. Apple’s security advisory confirms the update arrived on August 6 and fixes CVE-2026-65400.

Apple describes it as an authentication issue and says improved state management fixed it. The public CVE record classifies the flaw as improper authentication, while CISA’s enrichment gives it a 7.1 High severity score.

The advisory does not say the flaw has been exploited in the wild. Apple credits Alfredo Pesoli via Bynario Atlas for reporting it.

Sequoia and Sonoma get the same fix

If your Mac does not support macOS Tahoe 26, Apple has also released macOS Sequoia 15.7.9 and macOS Sonoma 14.8.9. Both updates patch the same Screen Sharing vulnerability.

Apple’s CVE record lists versions earlier than Tahoe 26.6.1, Sequoia 15.7.9, and Sonoma 14.8.9 as affected. That means staying on the previous 26.6, 15.7.8, or 14.8.8 release leaves the bug unpatched.

Update now or turn off Screen Sharing temporarily

Open System Settings > General > Software Update and install the update offered for your Mac. Apple lists Tahoe 26.6.1 as the latest macOS release, and this point update is focused on security rather than new features.

The risk matters because the built-in Screen Sharing feature can give another computer access to view and control your Mac. If you cannot update immediately and do not need the feature, open System Settings > General > Sharing and turn off Screen Sharing until the patch is installed.

Macs managed by a workplace or school may have different remote-access settings. In that case, follow your administrator’s instructions rather than changing a managed setting yourself.

title.rendered: ChatGPT gets a GPT-5.6 Sol reasoning slider as Luna expands free chats

content.rendered:
OpenAI is rolling out a revised GPT-5.6 experience in ChatGPT that gives eligible paid users direct control over reasoning effort. At the same time, GPT-5.6 Luna is becoming the default model for Free and Go users.

The distinction matters: free users are not getting OpenAI’s flagship Sol model. They are getting the faster, lower-cost Luna model for regular text chats and, starting next week, a Think button for harder questions.

Paid users can choose how much ChatGPT reasons

The new slider lets Plus and Pro users move between quicker answers and deeper reasoning without picking from a long list of model names.

The lowest Instant setting still runs on GPT-5.5 Instant. Medium and High use GPT-5.6 Sol, while Extra High is available on eligible higher-tier plans. The Pro setting uses GPT-5.6 Sol Pro for difficult or longer-running tasks.

ChatGPT can also switch automatically from Instant to Medium when a question needs more reasoning. OpenAI says those automatic switches do not use the separate allowance for manually selected reasoning.

That setup is clearer than asking people to understand every model tier. A quick question can stay on Instant, while research, planning, writing, coding, or a complicated decision can get more reasoning through the same control.

Free users get Luna, not Sol

GPT-5.6 Luna is rolling out as the default model for Free and Go users. OpenAI describes Luna as the fastest and most affordable member of the GPT-5.6 family, below the balanced Terra model and flagship Sol.

9to5Mac reports that OpenAI is offering unlimited Luna-backed text chats to free users. OpenAI’s current help page uses more careful language: it says free-tier access to GPT-5.5 Instant remains limited within a five-hour window and that limits can change based on demand, safeguards, and individual usage.

In other words, “unlimited” does not mean unlimited access to Sol or GPT-5.5 Instant. It refers to basic text chat continuing on Luna, while premium models and other features keep their own allowances.

Free and Go users will also get a Think button powered by Luna. It gives the model more time for a difficult question without moving the user to Sol. OpenAI says that rollout starts next week.

Work, Codex, and Apple Intelligence are separate

This update is for standard ChatGPT conversations. OpenAI says model availability in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API is unchanged, so existing plan limits and model choices still apply there.

The announcement also does not describe a change to the separate ChatGPT extension used by Siri and Apple Intelligence on iPhone. For now, the practical difference is inside ChatGPT itself: paid users get a simpler reasoning control, while free users move to Luna for everyday chat.

title.rendered: These 10 cinematic Odyssey wallpapers for iPhone that look absolutely stunning in 4K

content.rendered:
I just finished watching Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey and was completely mesmerized by the sweeping ocean voyages, towering fortresses, fearless warriors, and quiet moments before battles. Naturally, the first thing I wanted was an iPhone wallpaper that captured the same epic feeling every time I unlocked my phone.

That is the exact reason I’ve prepared this collection for you. Every background looks like it comes from the ancient Greek epic. If you’re still thinking about The Odyssey and want your iPhone to reflect that adventurous, cinematic vibe, these wallpapers are the perfect way to keep the journey going.

Download Odyssey Wallpaper Collection in 4K 

I have curated wallpapers from amazing creators on X (formerly Twitter) like @ArsivWallpaper, @koreanoli, @Cine vichaar, and more. Also, the collection includes our in-house designs from the CrestWall app.

1. The Silent Warrior 

A mysterious warrior stands with his back turned, overlooking a battlefield beneath dark blue storm clouds. The black helmet, braided crest, and distant army create an atmosphere of anticipation rather than action. The minimal composition also leaves plenty of room for your lock screen clock and widgets.

Download

2. Guardian of the Burning Gates 

Standing before massive burning gates, this heavily armored soldier looks ready for the final stand. The glowing orange fortress contrasts beautifully against the dark armor, giving my Lock Screen a cinematic movie-poster appearance.

If you like dramatic lighting and powerful warrior aesthetics, this is one of the strongest wallpapers in the collection.

Download

3. The Odyssey official movie poster wallpaper 

Here comes the official poster for The Odyssey. It captures one of the movie’s most intense moments of Odysseus’s brutal encounter with the Laestrygonians. I will say no more, as it may become a spoiler!

Its cinematic dark color palette makes it a striking choice for fans who want to celebrate the film itself.

Download

4. First look from The Odyssey 

Next wallpaper features an official first-look promotional image from The Odyssey. I loved Matt Damon as Odysseus, so this backdrop is special to me.

The aura of the battle-weary King of Ithaca with the warm cinematic lighting and intimate composition makes it one of the most memorable Depth Effect wallpapers.

Download

5. Telemachus waiting for his father 

Tom Holland as Telemachus, the son of Odysseus, is pure eye candy in the movie. As his father remains lost at sea after the Trojan War, Telemachus is left behind in Ithaca. Gazing across the endless ocean alone, the scene beautifully reflects his hope and loneliness.

I feel like this is one of the most emotional and visually striking wallpapers in the collection.

Download

6. King Agamemnon during the sack of Troy 

Instead of focusing on the chaos of war, this wallpaper centers on Benny Safdie’s portrayal of King Agamemnon, standing confidently as Troy burns behind him. The glowing fortress, towering gates, and dark armor make the entire scene feel larger than life.

If you enjoyed the opening moments of The Odyssey, download this wallpaper to give your iPhone a bold, cinematic look with the intensity of the Trojan War.

Download

7. Odysseus Faces Charybdis 

The next wallpaper brings another unforgettable moment from The Odyssey to life. It shows Odysseus steering his ship toward Charybdis, the legendary sea monster in Homer’s epic.

I love how the scene balances danger with determination and a beautiful landscape. If adventure is what drew you to The Odyssey, this is the wallpaper I’d recommend the most.

Download

8. Army of Greek hoplites

Instead of focusing on a single hero, the wallpaper showcases a formation of ancient Greek hoplite soldiers standing shoulder to shoulder, ready for battle. It instantly reminded me of the discipline and unity that defined the Greek armies in The Odyssey. 

Download

9. The fallen Spartan helmet 

This is one of my favorite wallpapers in the collection because it tells an entire story without showing a single character.

A lone Spartan-style helmet half-buried in wet sand beside the sea, symbolizing the cost of war and the uncertain journey that awaits Odysseus after Troy falls.

Download

10. Antinous in the Great Hall 

Lastly, the Odyssey wallpaper collection is incomplete without Antinous. He, along with a horde of suitors, takes over Odysseus’ palace during his long absence and indulges in the kingdom’s wealth without remorse.  

I like how this wallpaper stands out from the others. The warm tavern-like lighting and Pattinson’s confident expression give it a cinematic look that’s perfect for a lock screen. 

Download

Why The Odyssey wallpapers look great on iPhone 

Not every wallpaper looks good once it’s stretched across an iPhone screen, but The Odyssey collection feels like it was made for it. The vertical compositions naturally fit the iPhone’s display, while the cinematic lighting and rich colors make every wallpaper stand out on both the Lock Screen and Home Screen.

Another reason these wallpapers work so well is their use of contrast. Dark skies, glowing firelight, bronze armor, and deep blue oceans create a dramatic look that especially shines on OLED displays.

Beyond the visuals, each wallpaper tells part of Odysseus’ journey. It may be Matt Damon as the tired King of Ithaca, Tom Holland as the aspiring Telemachus, Agamemnon commanding to sack Troy, or even the Spartan helmet washing ashore – all these wallpapers feel as if taken straight from Christopher Nolan’s epic.

Keep the epic journey alive on your iPhone

Whether you’re counting down to watch Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey or you’ve already fallen in love with Homer’s legendary tale, these wallpapers will be perfect to bring that adventure onto your iPhone.

From Odysseus’ perilous voyage and Telemachus’ unwavering hope to the fall of Troy and the tension inside Ithaca, every wallpaper shows one of these memorable moments from the epic story. Download your favorites in 4K and give your Lock Screen a cinematic upgrade for free.

And if you’re looking for even more exclusive, high-quality wallpapers inspired by movies, anime, games, and pop culture, don’t forget to explore the CrestWall app for fresh in-house designs updated regularly.
