title.rendered: I finally found USB-C cables that are actually worth buying for iPhone

content.rendered:
I used to think every USB-C cable was basically the same. Nevertheless, in the process of purchasing a new USB-C cable for my iPhone 17, I discovered that there are significant differences in speed, reliability, performance, and even convenience.

Some cables are built only for charging, while others can transfer 10Gbps files, connect an external monitor, or survive years of daily use. After comparing the latest options, these are the USB-C cables I’d confidently recommend for different types of iPhone users.

Whether you own an iPhone 15, iPhone 16, or the latest iPhone 17 series, this guide will help you choose the right cable instead of wasting money on one that won’t meet your needs.

How I chose these USB-C cables

The biggest truth is that the most expensive cables aren’t always the best ones. Many cables promise ultra-fast charging or massive 240W power delivery, but most iPhone users will never come close to using that much power. Instead of chasing marketing claims, I focused on the features that actually make a difference in everyday use.

Here’s what I paid the closest attention to before recommending these cables.

I picked cable length based on real-world use

One thing I underestimated was how much cable length changes the overall experience.

  • 3 ft (1 m) cables are my go-to for desks, travel, and power banks because they stay tidy and don’t leave extra cable hanging everywhere.
  • 6 ft (2 m) cables are what I’d recommend for most people. They’re long enough to comfortably use your iPhone from the couch or bed while charging.
  • 10 ft (3 m) cables can be incredibly convenient if your outlet is far away, but longer cables may introduce a slight drop in charging performance depending on the cable’s quality.

Rather than calling one length “best,” I chose cables that fit different lifestyles.

Build quality matters more than fancy marketing

A charging cable gets bent, twisted, packed in a backpack, and tied up almost every day. That is why I paid more attention to durability over flashy packaging.

The cables on this list include features like:

  • Braided nylon exteriors
  • Reinforced strain relief near the connectors
  • Metal connector housings
  • High bend-life ratings, often between 10,000 and 30,000 bends

These details may not sound exciting, but they’re usually what separates a cable that lasts for years from one that frays after a few months.

I didn’t get distracted by 240W claims

You’ll see USB-C cables advertised with 60W, 100W, or even 240W charging support. While those numbers look impressive, they’re not the deciding factor for an iPhone.

Current iPhones top out at roughly 40-30W of charging, so even a 60W cable has plenty of headroom. I still included cables of higher rating because they could charge not only an iPhone, but also an iPad or MacBook, or other USB-C devices, making them a smarter long-term investment if you want one cable for everything.

Data speed is where USB-C cables really differ

This was probably the biggest surprise during my research. Two USB-C cables can look identical but perform very differently.

  • USB 2.0 cables max out at 480 Mbps and are perfectly fine if you only charge your iPhone.
  • USB 3.2 cables can transfer data at up to 10 Gbps, making them much better for moving photos and videos.
  • USB4 and Thunderbolt 4 cables reach 40 Gbps and are designed for creators who work with external SSDs, ProRes video, or high-resolution monitors.

If you regularly transfer large files from your iPhone Pro or use external storage, investing in a faster cable is well worth it. Otherwise, a standard USB 2.0 cable will do the job just fine.

I only considered trusted brands

Finally, I avoided no-name cables with vague specifications. Every recommendation in this guide comes from a reputable brand that includes important safety features like E-marker chips, intelligent power management, and thermal protection.

Such measures help to control power delivery, prevent overheating, and keep your iPhone’s battery safe for a long period. Saving a few dollars on an uncertified cable simply isn’t worth the potential risk.

At the end of the day, I wasn’t looking for the cable with the highest specs on paper. Instead, I chose cables that offer the best combination of reliability, durability, charging performance, and long-term value for the way most people actually use their iPhones.

Best USB-C cables for iPhone I’d recommend in 2026

1. Apple USB-C charge cable: Best for reliable everyday charging

  • Charging: 60W and 240W
  • Length: 1m (3 ft) or 2m (6.6 ft)
  • Data Transfer: USB 2.0 (480Mbps)

Apple’s own cable is still the safest choice if you simply want dependable charging without worrying about compatibility. It feels premium, supports standard high power delivery, and works perfectly with every USB-C iPhone.

What I like most is the 2-meter length. It’s long enough that I wouldn’t feel tethered to the wall while using my iPhone on the couch or in bed. Apple also replaced its older rubber coating with a woven braided exterior, which should hold up much better against everyday bends, twists, and the inevitable trips into backpacks and desk drawers.

But I wouldn’t buy this cable if fast file transfers are a priority. Despite the premium price, it still tops out at USB 2.0 (480 Mbps), so moving large ProRes videos or photo libraries will take noticeably longer.

For me, this cable is all about peace of mind. If I wanted one dependable cable that works seamlessly across my iPhone, iPad, AirPods, and MacBook without wondering about compatibility or build quality, Apple’s own cable would still be near the top of my list.

Pros

  • Official Apple accessory with guaranteed compatibility
  • Durable woven braided design
  • Long 6.6 ft (2 m) cable is ideal for bedside charging
  • Supports up to 240W USB-C Power Delivery for future-proofing

Cons

  • Slow USB 2.0 transfer
  • Costs more than many equally durable third-party alternatives

Best for: If you want a dependable, long-lasting USB-C cable for everyday charging and don’t need ultra-fast data transfer.

Check out on Amazon

2. Anker Nano USB-C Cable: The one I’d recommend to almost everyone

  • Charging: Up to 240W
  • Length: 1ft, 3ft, 6ft, and 10ft
  • Data Transfer: USB 2.0

If I had to recommend just one cable to most people, it would be the Anker Nano.

Anker has always done a great job balancing quality and price, and the Nano USB-C Cable offers a great balance of durability, flexibility, and long-term value. What immediately stands out is how soft and flexible the cable feels. Anker also rates it for up to 30,000 bends, and the recycled nylon exterior is designed to handle daily wear while staying tangle-resistant.

The 240W Power Delivery support is honestly more than an iPhone will ever need, but that’s exactly why I like it. You can keep one cable for your iPhone, iPad, MacBook, CarPlay, gaming handheld, or almost any USB-C device. Moreover, the USB-IF certification ensures zero damage. The only compromise is the 480 Mbps data speed.

Pros

  • Soft, flexible braided design that’s easy to carry
  • Supports CarPlay
  • Includes a silicone cord organizer for neat wrapping
  • Beautiful color options

Cons

  • Expensive
  • Overkill if you only ever charge an iPhone

Best for: Anyone looking for one durable USB-C cable that can charge an iPhone today and still handle more demanding USB-C devices in the future.

Check out on Amazon

3. LISEN USB-C to USB-C Cable: The budget pick that doesn’t feel cheap

  • Charging: Up to 240W
  • Length: 1.6 ft, 3.3 ft, 6.6 ft, 10 ft
  • Data Transfer: USB 2.0

When I’m shopping for a charging cable on a budget, I’m usually skeptical. Most inexpensive cables either feel flimsy or have loose connectors. The LISEN 240W USB-C Cable is one of the few exceptions.

What impressed me most is that LISEN didn’t cut corners where it matters. It has a braided 48-strand military-grade nylon exterior that is rated to withstand 40,000 bends and remain tug-resistant. Additionally, the reinforced connectors ensure reliable charging and support for up to 240W Power Delivery, which handles all your Apple gear.

You can choose up to a 10 ft length to comfortably reach from a wall outlet to your bed, couch, or desk without feeling restrictive. Of course, there are a few compromises. Like many charging-focused USB-C cables, it only supports USB 2.0 data transfer speeds.

Pros

  • Excellent value for the price
  • Supports up to 240W fast charging
  • Durable braided nylon construction
  • Long length options

Cons

  • Limited data speed
  • Design is more functional than premium

Best for: If your goal is simply fast, reliable charging without spending a premium, this is one of the strongest value picks

Check out on Amazon

4. UGREEN USB-C Cable with Display: See what’s happening behind

  • Charging: Up to 240W
  • Length: 3.3 ft, 6.6 ft, 10 ft
  • Data Transfer: USB 2.0

Most USB-C cables leave you guessing whether your phone is actually fast charging. The UGREEN Digital Display Cable removes that guesswork with a small LED screen built into the connector that cycles through real-time wattage, voltage, and current.

I liked how this cable combines a genuinely useful feature with premium construction. The 24-strand braided nylon jacket, aluminum connector housing, built-in E-Marker chip, and 240W PD 3.1 support make it feel like a cable that’s built to last. However, you should use a high-wattage power adapter to enjoy the fastest speeds.

The only thing I’d keep in mind is that this is still a USB 2.0 cable, so its 480 Mbps data speed is aimed at charging rather than moving massive video files. Also, because the display stays lit while charging, I find it a little too bright for a bedside setup.

Pros

  • Built-in LED display shows wattage, voltage, and current
  • Supports PD 3.1 fast charging for all modern USB-C devices
  • Built-in E-Marker chip for safe, stable charging
  • Great conversation starter for any desk setup

Cons

  • No color option
  • Display isn’t essential for everyone

Best for: Power users and tech enthusiasts who want to monitor their charging speed in real time.

Check out on Amazon

5. Rolling Square inCharge XL Multi Charging Cable: Best for traveling

  • Charging: Up to 100W
  • Length: 1 ft
  • Data Transfer: USB 2.0

If I could only throw one charging cable into my backpack before a trip, this would probably be it.

What makes the Rolling Square inCharge XL different is its versatility. Instead of carrying separate cables for an iPhone, AirPods, older accessories, or a laptop, this single cable combines six different connection combinations. You get USB-C and USB-A inputs along with USB-C, Lightning, and Micro-USB outputs.

It supports up to 100W USB-C Power Delivery, enough to fast-charge an iPhone, iPad, MacBook Air, or many laptops. Moreover, I tried its OTG phone-to-phone charging. The cable uses a braided nylon exterior, silicone protective cap, reinforced copper wiring, and even includes strong magnets that keep it snapped together when it’s not in use.

Pros

  • Extremely portable and clever design
  • Six connection combinations in one cable
  • Premium braided construction with magnetic cable management
  • Perfect for travel, commuting, and shared charging setups

Cons

  • More expensive
  • Not ideal as a permanent desk cable

Best for: Travelers, remote workers, and anyone who wants one cable that can charge almost every device they carry without filling their bag with adapters.

Check out on Amazon

6. Cable Matters USB4 Cable: The one I’d buy for ProRes, external SSDs, and future-proofing

  • Charging: Up to 240W
  • Length: 3 ft, 6 ft, 8.2 ft
  • Data Transfer: USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 (Up to 20Gbps)
  • Monitor Support: Yes (up to 8K)

If your USB-C cable is only for charging an iPhone, this is probably more cable than you’ll ever need. But if you transfer large files, work with external SSDs, connect to a monitor, or use a USB dock, this is the cable I’d spend extra money on.

With 20Gbps bandwidth, it can transfer massive video projects in seconds instead of minutes, while also supporting DisplayPort Alt Mode for connecting to external monitors at resolutions up to 8K. It also supports 100W USB Power Delivery, making it capable of charging everything from an iPhone to a MacBook with a single cable.

I also appreciate that Cable Matters doesn’t cut corners on certification. This cable is USB-IF certified. That gives me more confidence when using it with expensive devices or external storage. The only downside is that this cable feels noticeably thicker and stiffer.

If you only charge your iPhone overnight, you’re paying for features you’ll probably never use. But if your iPhone is part of a professional workflow, this cable quickly justifies its price.

Pros

  • Lightning-fast 20Gbps USB4 data transfe
  • Supports external displays up to 8K via DisplayPort Alt Mode
  • USB-IF certified for reliability and compatibility
  • Backward compatible with USB-C, USB 3.2, and Thunderbolt devices

Cons

  • Costs significantly more than standard charging cables
  • Thicker and less flexible than everyday USB-C cables
  • Overkill if you only use your cable for charging

Best for: Creators, photographers, videographers, and iPhone Pro users.

Check out on Amazon

7. Baseus Retractable USB-C Cable: It finally fixed my desk clutter

  • Charging: Up to 100W
  • Length: Adjustable up to 6.6ft with 4 preset lengths
  • Data Transfer: USB 2.0

After looking at dozens of USB-C cables, I realized one thing: performance isn’t always the biggest annoyance. Cable clutter is.

That’s exactly why the Baseus Retractable USB-C Cable caught my attention. Instead of leaving a loose cable stretched across your desk or tangled inside your backpack, it retracts neatly into a compact housing. I could simply pull it to the four preset lengths as required and give it another gentle pull to retract it back inside.

Despite the retractable mechanism, Baseus says it’s been tested for 50,000 pull cycles, which is reassuring. Of course, this isn’t a cable built for professional work. It only supports 480 Mbps data transfers. Still, if your biggest frustration is constantly untangling charging cables or dealing with a messy desk, I think this is one of the smartest designs on this list.

Pros

  • Retractable design keeps desks and bags clutter-free
  • Four adjustable cable lengths for different situations
  • Compact and travel-friendly
  • Rated for thousands of retraction cycles for long-term durability 

Cons

  • Retractable housing is bulkier than a standard cable

Best for: Anyone who values a clean workspace or travels frequently and wants a USB-C cable that’s easy to store without sacrificing fast charging.

Check out on Amazon

8. Statik MagStack magnetic USB-C Cable: The smartest cable for keeping your desk organized

  • Charging: Up to 100W
  • Length: 3.3 ft, 6.6 ft
  • Data Transfer: 480 Mbps

Another cable that solves the tangling and clutter problem. Instead of relying on Velcro straps or cable ties, the Statik MagStack has built-in magnets running through the cable, allowing it to snap together automatically into a neat coil.

It stays organized in my backpack, wraps around a charger in seconds, and even sticks to metal surfaces like a desk frame or filing cabinet. Statik also uses a reinforced nylon braid and aluminum connectors, giving the cable a premium feel while improving durability.

What I appreciate most is that this cable solves an everyday problem. In case your office table keeps getting cluttered with charging cables or your travel bag becomes a knot of wires, the magnetic design genuinely makes life easier.

Pros

  • Built-in magnets automatically keep the cable neatly coiled
  • Durable braided nylon construction
  • Easy to organize in backpacks, desks, and cable drawers

Cons

  • Premium pricing

Best for: Anyone who hates tangled charging cables and wants the easiest cable to organize at home, in the office, or while traveling.

Check out on Amazon

9. AINOPE Right Angle USB-C Cable: Best for gaming & CarPlay

  • Charging: Up to 240W
  • Length: 1.5 ft, 3.3 ft, 6.6 ft, 10 ft, and 15 ft
  • Data Transfer: USB 2.0

Out of all the cables on this list, this is probably the one with the most practical design. I tried it out of curiosity, but the 90-degree right-angle connector completely changed how comfortable the cable feels when I am watching YouTube, scrolling social media, or playing games while it’s charging, or using wired Apple CarPlay.

A regular straight connector sticks out from the bottom of the phone and often gets in the way of your hand. The AINOPE cable routes the wire to the side instead, putting less strain on both the connector and the charging port while making the phone much easier to hold.

In terms of performance, this cable is compatible with up to 240W USB PD 3.0/PD 3.1 and QC 3.0, providing fast charging for your iPhone as well as all USB-C devices. Other notable features include a double-braided nylon jacket, reinforced strain relief, laser-welded connectors, and an integrated E-Marker chip for safe power negotiation.

Pros

  • Durable double-braided nylon construction
  • Reinforced strain relief
  • Excellent for gaming, streaming, Apple CarPlay, and everyday use

Cons

  • Right-angle design may not suit every charging setup

Best for: Gaming and in-car charging.

Check out on Amazon

Things I learned about testing these USB-C cables

The biggest surprise was how different USB-C cables have become.

A few lessons stood out:

  • Expensive doesn’t always mean better.
  • Most people don’t need a 240W cable.
  • Braided cables generally last longer than basic plastic ones.
  • If you only charge your iPhone, USB 2.0 cables are perfectly fine.
  • USB4 cables are worth buying only if you regularly transfer huge files or use external storage.
  • Convenience features like retractable cables, magnetic storage, or power displays make charging your device more convenient on a day-to-day basis.

Choosing the right cable is more about your daily habits than chasing the highest specifications.

Which cable should you buy?

Here’s my recommendation based on different needs:

Get the right Type-C cable for your iPhone!

USB-C has finally simplified charging across devices, but choosing the right cable still matters. A well-made cable can last for years, charge more reliably, and even unlock faster data transfers if you need them.

For most iPhone owners, the Anker Nano USB-C Cable strikes the best balance between price, durability, and everyday performance. If you need something more specialized—whether it’s a USB4 cable for professional workflows, a retractable option for a tidy desk, or a travel-friendly all-in-one solution—there’s a cable here that fits the job.

Is there a USB-C cable you think deserves a spot on this list? Share your recommendation in the comments below!

@graph.name: Apple USB-C to USB-C Woven Charge Cable
@graph.description: Apple’s woven USB-C cable is lightweight, soft, tangle-resistant, and consistent. The braided design adds better durability than the older plastic version, and its compatibility is flawless across all Apple devices.

@graph.name: Anker 310 Type-C Fast Charging Cable
@graph.description: Anker has built its reputation on dependable cables at friendly prices. This cable includes braided nylon for strength, aluminum shielding, TPE insulation, and reinforced connectors. It handles up to 10,000 bends and is USB-IF compliant for safe charging.

@graph.name: Belkin BoostCharge USB-C to USB-C Power Cable
@graph.description: If you are looking for a USB-C cable for fast charging your iPhone, iPad, and MacBook Pro, this Belkin BoostCharge cable is perfect. It offers premium build quality, including a durable anodized aluminum cable head and a double-braided nylon cable. The brand claims it can survive over 30,000 bends and 10,000 plug-ins.

@graph.name: Cable Matters Gen 2 USB-C Cable
@graph.description: The Cable Matters USB-C to USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 cable provides seamless video and data for streaming, gaming, or professional use.

@graph.name: UGREEN USB-C to USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 Cable
@graph.description: UGREEN has become a well-respected brand for high-value electronics accessories. Their USB-C cables are rugged due to the shielded wire mesh, TPE, and double-braided nylon cover. The high-power throughput goes up to 240W, suitable for all USB-C/Thunderbolt 3 devices.

@graph.name: Baseus Retractable USB-C Cable
@graph.description: If you want a super portable and compact yet lengthy Type-C cable, get this Baseus one. It is 6.6ft long but retractable in a small, 0.9-inch-tall round storage. So, no more messy tangled cables or bending issues. The cable has a 7-stage length preset to let you pull the required cable.

title.rendered: Meta launches Muse Code for Mac with cheaper pricing if it can train on your data

content.rendered:
Meta has launched Muse Code, a beta AI coding agent that runs in Terminal on macOS and Linux. It is powered by the new Muse Spark 1.2 model and can plan changes, edit code, validate its work, and coordinate multiple background agents across large repositories.

There is no dedicated Mac app. Meta provides a one-line installer, after which developers work with Muse Code from the command line:

curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | bash

Muse Code is built for long-running work

Muse Code keeps specialized background agents active throughout a session instead of starting a new one for every small task. Meta says this avoids repeated research and reduces the amount of steering needed during complicated jobs.

It also records every model call, tool run, approval, and edit in a local append-only event log. If Muse Code or the computer crashes, the agent can replay that log and continue from where it stopped.

Three bundled commands show the kind of workflow Meta is targeting. /plan creates a plan that needs approval, /grill stress-tests that plan, and /goal keeps the agent working toward a specified objective.

Muse Spark 1.2 is a coding-focused update to Muse Spark 1.1. Meta says it improves code generation, debugging, codebase understanding, and end-to-end development. The model was trained for longer jobs, including complete repository generation and projects that need planning and context compression.

Meta’s published evaluation charts put Muse Spark 1.2 at 82.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 59.3% on DeepSWE 1.1, and 70.6% on Meta Internal Coding Bench. It did not lead any of the three charts: Opus 5 topped Terminal-Bench and Meta’s internal test, while GPT 5.6 Terra led DeepSWE. These are Meta-published results, and the internal benchmark is not independently verifiable.

The cheaper tier lets Meta train on your prompts

The biggest catch is in the pricing. MacRumors reports that Meta offers Standard and Contributor access, with a steep discount for developers who let the company use their prompts and completions to train future AI models.

The reported rates are for one million tokens:

That makes Contributor pricing 12.5 times cheaper for input and a little over 21 times cheaper for output. The tradeoff is not subtle: developers pay far less, but Meta gets permission to learn from what they send and receive.

The Contributor tier may suit experiments and public code. Private repositories, client work, API keys, and unreleased products need more caution. For that work, the Standard tier’s higher price buys the more important feature: keeping coding sessions out of future model training.

Meta joins the Codex and Claude Code race

Muse Code is Meta’s most direct answer yet to OpenAI Codex and Anthropic’s Claude Code. All three are moving beyond code completion toward agents that can inspect a project, make changes, test the result, and keep working with less supervision.

The competition on Mac is already moving quickly. OpenAI recently added Appshots to Codex for Mac for sharing app context, while Claude Code gained iOS Simulator support for building and testing iPhone apps.

Meta’s entry is more developer-focused than the consumer tools in its growing Muse family, which also includes Muse Image. Muse Spark 1.2 is available through Muse Code and the Meta Model API with expanded global access.

Muse Code is still in beta, and its Terminal-only setup will make it less approachable than a normal Mac app. For developers comfortable with the command line, the harder decision is whether the Contributor discount is worth letting Meta train on their coding sessions.

title.rendered: Abode adds Apple Home-compatible sensors for garages and gates

content.rendered:
Abode has launched a $34.99 Garage Tilt Sensor and a $49.99 Outdoor Contact Sensor for monitoring garages, gates, sheds, and other entry points around a home.

Both can show their open or closed status in Apple Home and work with Alexa and Google Assistant. They also support Abode’s CUE automations, so an open gate could switch on driveway lights or a garage left open could trigger an alert.

There is one important catch: both sensors require an Abode security system. Apple Home support runs through the Abode hub, so these are mainly for people who already use or plan to buy into Abode’s setup.

One sensor reads a door’s angle

The Garage Tilt Sensor detects when a surface changes position by roughly 45 degrees. That makes it suitable for overhead garage doors, attic hatches, basement hopper windows, and other hinged panels where a regular two-piece contact sensor may not fit well.

It uses a replaceable CR123 lithium battery and sends low-battery alerts to your phone. Abode advertises a wireless range of more than 100 feet, which should help with detached garages and outbuildings.

The outdoor sensor is built for gates and sheds

The Outdoor Contact Sensor uses a stronger magnet and allows a wider gap between its two parts. Abode says it can be mounted on wood or metal surfaces, including gates, sheds, storage units, mailboxes, and detached garages.

Its IP66 rating means it is dust-tight and designed to withstand strong water jets. It runs on two AA batteries and is rated for temperatures from -13°F to 140°F.

For Apple users, the appeal is having these entry alerts appear alongside existing HomeKit smart home devices and HomeKit Secure Video cameras. That adds coverage beyond the doors and windows most indoor sensors monitor.

Both new Abode sensors are available now from the company’s online store.

title.rendered: What is Placeholder in Fortnite? Here’s the answer

content.rendered:
Recently, Fortnite OG Season 9 sparked discussion among players after the word “Placeholder” unexpectedly appeared in several parts of the game, including at the start of matches. The unusual text quickly caught the community’s attention, with players sharing screenshots across social media and reporting the issue to Epic Games in hopes of finding out what it meant.

In programming terms, a placeholder is a temporary filler text that is meant to be replaced with the final text before release. In the final version. In Fortnite’s case, too, the placeholder text seems to have somehow emerged in a new update pushed into the game after most likely being included temporarily in the code.

The Placeholder issue in Fortnite

On July 30, initial reports started piling up about Fortnite fans spotting the “Placeholder” text at the beginning of a match. This incident understandably took place during the Peely Hours, an in-game event during which the Peely Sprite spawn rate was boosted.

Places on the screen where texts such as “Peely Hours”, “Peely Everywhere”, and “Peely Sprite Drop Rate Up” should have appeared instead showed “Placeholder”—creating an amusing effect for the audience. This goof-up by Epic devs was, as expected, not ignored by players who tuned in around that time, leading to a flurry of posts poking fun at the same.

PLACEHOLDER STARTED 😭😭 pic.twitter.com/xaGxf9GeAc

— Backers | Fortnite News (@BackersGamesF) July 30, 2026

In the comments of those posts, several different X users had a laugh at Fortnite’s expense. One user named Josh Wazowski insinuated that someone was “getting yelled at over this,” whereas another user, Openminded187, jokingly stated that it was “the most fitting event name” Epic Games had come up with.

As soon as the news of the placeholder issue broke out, the team behind Fortnite noticed it swiftly and acknowledged the issue. In an hour or so after that, the text was reportedly fixed in the game, and players started seeing what was originally intended to appear in those areas.

Wrapping up

As in all facets of life, mistakes occasionally show up even in AAA video games like Fortnite. After all, it is human to err. The placeholder issue was similarly a direct result of possibly a complacent proofread before deploying the code onto the server. Given that it was patched up as soon as it was detected and was something that only appeared during the Peely Hours, which are long over now, you shouldn’t expect to come across this issue in the game again.

However, there are certain other common issues in Epic’s multiplayer title that crop up every now and then. Among them, the “Pak is invalid” Fortnite error is arguably closer to the top of the list of most annoying issues faced by players. In case you want to know more about this error, in order to stay prepared for when it strikes, you can check out the guide linked above.

FAQs

Is the Placeholder text issue temporary in Fortnite?

Yes, it was a temporary issue, which was fixed soon after reports came in.

Is Placeholder a Fortnite bug?

It is not a bug but only a small oversight that crept into the final version of the recent Fortnite update.

How many players were affected by the recent Placeholder text issue?

There are no such numbers publicly available, but it is fair to assume that the issue affected everyone in Fortnite during the Peely Hours event.

  • How to enable Fortnite 2FA and secure your account
  • How to get the Sir Wyvern sidekick in Fortnite

title.rendered: WhatsApp is developing an AI-content label for Channel updates

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is developing a new label that would let Channel admins flag media created or edited with AI. WABetaInfo found the feature in WhatsApp beta for Android 2.26.31.1, but it is still under development and is not available to beta testers.

The label would give followers a visible warning when a Channel update contains AI-generated media. For now, it appears to be a manual disclosure tool rather than a system that automatically detects AI content.

How the AI content label would work

After posting an update, a Channel admin would press and hold the message, open the context menu, and select Add AI content label. A visible label would then appear on the message bubble. The report says admins may not be able to remove it once added.

The option is expected to cover images, videos, and other media created or edited with any AI tool, not only Meta AI. Text appears to be treated differently: WABetaInfo says AI-assisted writing, including text drafted with WhatsApp’s Writing Help feature, may not require the same label.

That distinction matters because WhatsApp Channels are one-way broadcasts used by creators, organizations, and businesses to reach large groups of followers. A clear label could help people judge realistic images or videos without leaving the update.

A public rollout is not confirmed

WABetaInfo reports that WhatsApp is also working on the feature for iPhone, although the current evidence comes from the Android beta. WhatsApp has not announced the label, confirmed where it will be required, or given a release date.

The timing follows the EU AI Act becoming generally applicable on August 2. Article 50 of the law includes disclosure rules for certain AI-generated or manipulated media. WABetaInfo says WhatsApp is building the label to help Channel admins meet legal requirements in some countries, but WhatsApp has not publicly tied the feature to a specific regulation.

The reported workflow also mirrors the paid-partnership labels used for sponsored Channel updates. WhatsApp has already expanded the Updates tab with promoted Channels and Status ads, so the AI label would extend its disclosure tools beyond advertising.

Nothing changes for users yet. If WhatsApp moves the feature into testing, its first rollout should clarify which media needs a label, whether admins can remove one, and whether availability depends on local law.

excerpt.rendered: WhatsApp may let Channel admins add visible labels to AI-generated media. The feature is still under development, with no confirmed rollout date.

title.rendered: Disney CEO confirms a free Disney+ tier is under consideration

content.rendered:
Disney is considering a free, ad-supported way to watch Disney+, CEO Josh D’Amaro confirmed during the company’s Q3 FY26 earnings call. For anyone tired of adding another monthly subscription, the idea sounds promising—but it is not a launch announcement.

D’Amaro said a free product could help Disney reach more price-sensitive viewers, create additional inventory for advertisers, and bring potential subscribers into Disney+. He also made clear that the company has nothing specific to announce yet.

That means there is no launch date, list of supported countries, or word on which movies and shows would be available for free.

Disney has not said what viewers would get

Disney+ currently offers only paid plans. In the U.S., the With Ads plan costs $11.99 per month, while Premium costs $18.99 per month or $189.99 per year. Disney also says it does not offer a free trial.

If a free option launches, ads would pay for it. Disney has not explained how it would differ from the existing paid With Ads plan, so it is too early to know whether viewers would get a smaller catalog, limited episodes, or something else.

The model itself is familiar. Free services such as Tubi already trade a monthly fee for regular advertising. A Disney+ free tier would also give the company a broader no-cost entry point than subscription services such as Apple TV.

The idea has moved beyond an internal discussion

Business Insider reported in July that Disney product and technology chief Adam Smith had discussed free-tier content during an internal streaming meeting. At the time, the report said Disney had shared neither a timeline nor the scope of the possible offering.

D’Amaro’s public comments confirm that the idea remains active. They also show why Disney is interested: its latest shareholder letter says streaming ad revenue rose 3% year over year in the quarter, while subscription revenue grew 15%.

A free tier could expand both sides of that business by adding more ad-supported viewing and introducing Disney+ to people who will not pay upfront. Until Disney shares a product or launch plan, free Disney+ remains an idea, not an option.

title.rendered: Fortnite teases new Bleach collab: Yoruichi skin and more confirmed

content.rendered:
Bleach has returned to Fortnite for a second stint in the Item Shop, attracting fans of the highly popular anime to the online multiplayer game. As formal confirmation of the same, the official Fortnite X account recently shared a teaser, giving everyone a glimpse of what’s to come.

The coveted Japanese IP’s first partnership with the Epic-developed title took place in December 2025. In the original run, Bleach characters including Orihime Inoue, Rukia Kuchiki, Ichigo Kurosaki, and Uryu Ishida were enrolled in Fortnite’s skins catalog. Now, a new set of cosmetics is set to arrive soon in Wave 2 of the Fortnite x Bleach collab.

Fortnite x Bleach coming soon

On Tuesday, Fortnite officially confirmed that its latest collaboration with Bleach was set to unfold on August 7. Along with the schedule, a short teaser video showing Yoruichi Shihouin and Kisuke Urahara in action was also posted.

Don't blink. See you August 7. pic.twitter.com/llfwvQkjO8

— Fortnite (@Fortnite) August 4, 2026

In the comments, some Fortnite players expressed huge excitement, in particular about the addition of the Yoruichi skin. On the flipside, some fans took the opportunity to ask the devs for themed content related to other renowned anime IPs, One Piece and My Hero Academia. Moreover, they also suggested video game franchises, including Sonic The Hedgehog and Nier: Automata, as potential collab partners for the future.

Fortnite Bleach Wave 2 leaked content

Prior to the official confirmation, reputed leakers Shiina and HYPEX had leaked the arrival of Yoruichi and Kisuke in Fortnite. After their reports surfaced on July 30, more information was dished out by other insiders, giving a deeper look into the Wave 2 content for Fortnite x Bleach.

According to SpushFNBR, the Yoruichi Fortnite skin is set to come in two variants: Regular and Ninja. Similarly, Kisuke is rumored to have three different variants whose finer details are yet to be known. While Yoruichi is expected to be complemented with the Shunryu Kokubyo Arms pickaxe and Yoruichi Cape back bling, Kisuke is reported to get the Benihime pickaxe and Soul Candy back bling.

FORTNITE x BLEACH WAVE 2 SHOP COSMETIC INFORMATION 🔥

– Yoruichi Shihoin: Shunko Raijin Senkai style, Shunryu Kokubyo Arms Pickaxe (inspired by the cat-like form from the most recent episodes), Yoruichi Cape Backbling

– Kisuke Urahara: Multiple styles (one might be no hat, but… pic.twitter.com/vs8wvu7fJU

— SpushFNBR (@SpushFNBR) July 31, 2026

Another popular leaker, Loolo, shared that the Yoruichi skin will come with a God of Thunder style, inspired by the character’s recent escapades in the highly celebrated anime. This particular style is among the more requested attires for the iconic Bleach figure.

Rounding up

Since there are merely a couple of days left for the full reveal of Bleach Wave 2 content, Fortnite fans won’t have to fret over the rumors for too long. Given the considerably strong reception to the teaser so far, it won’t be a stretch to say players are certainly looking for this collab.

It will be interesting to see how accurately the aforementioned leaks translate into reality when the Fortnite x Bleach promotion finally drops. Further, judging by the general interest in the community, the Yoruichi Fortnite skin appears to be in pole position to top the Item Shop charts on Friday. Suffice to say, this weekend update is going to be a big one for fans of Bleach and Fortnite.

FAQs

When was the last Fortnite x Bleach collab?

The original Fortnite x Bleach collab happened during Chapter 7 Season 1 in December 2025.

What was included in Bleach Wave 1 items?

Among the Bleach Wave 1 additions were skins inspired by Orihime Inoue, Rukia Kuchiki, Ichigo Kurosaki, and Uryu Ishida, as well as themed pickaxes, back blings, emotes, wraps, and decals.

Which other popular anime has collaborated with Fortnite before?

Apart from Bleach, Dragon Ball, Naruto, Jujutsu Kaisen, Attack on Titan, and My Hero Academia have previously been featured in Fortnite.

  • How to get Squid Game skins in Fortnite
  • How to get Stranger Things skins in Fortnite
  • How to get X-Men skins in Fortnite
  • How to get Addison Rae skin in Fortnite

title.rendered: What do different icons and symbols mean on Claude?

content.rendered:
Claude puts dictation beside full Voice mode and three very different Cowork approval modes behind a hand, fast-forward, and warning symbol. Mixing them up can change how Claude handles your prompt or acts on your behalf.

This guide decodes the icons in Claude’s current web and desktop interface. Your layout may look slightly different depending on your device, plan, workspace settings, and Anthropic’s rollout. If you’re still deciding whether to switch AI tools, this hands-on ChatGPT vs Claude comparison explains the practical differences beyond the interface.

Claude chat box icons

The main composer combines chat modes, model controls, attachments, and two kinds of voice input. Here is what each symbol does.

The model and effort labels work together. Lower effort stretches your usage further for routine requests; higher effort is better saved for difficult work.

What the icons inside the plus menu mean

Clicking the plus button reveals more than attachments. It is also where Claude keeps search, Research, skills, connectors, and plugins.

The plain magnifying glass and the Research symbol are easy to mix up. A normal magnifying glass searches a list or page; Research asks Claude to investigate a topic through multiple searches.

Claude sidebar icons

The left sidebar is the quickest route to conversations, projects, generated work, schedules, and customization.

Chats and tasks page controls

The history page adds controls for finding and managing conversations.

Some sidebar items are plan-dependent. For example, the clock is tied to scheduled Cowork tasks, so it may not appear on every account.

Cowork project and approval symbols

Cowork can take actions instead of only replying with text, which is why its approval icons matter more than they first appear. You can also read how Claude Cowork works across iPhone, web, and desktop before handing it a larger task.

Cowork project picker symbols

Opening the Project menu reveals another small group of controls.

Stick with the hand icon until you understand the task. Automatically approve is a useful middle ground, while Skip all approvals removes the check that could catch an unsafe action.

Account menu icons

Click your profile initials in the lower-left corner to open account, plan, help, and app controls.

Icons in Claude Settings

Most Settings symbols repeat familiar ideas, but a few are specific to Claude’s products.

Other symbols on a Settings page

These controls appear in the main Settings panel rather than the navigation list.

The Usage bars show how much of each allowance you have consumed; they are not download progress bars. Claude’s usage dashboard updates consumption across supported Claude products.

The Claude symbols people confuse most

If you only remember five distinctions, make them these:

  • Microphone vs waveform: The microphone types what you say; the waveform begins a spoken conversation.
  • Ghost vs profile: The ghost starts an Incognito chat; your initials open the account menu.
  • Web search vs Research: Web search handles quick current questions; Research performs a broader investigation.
  • Hand vs fast-forward vs warning: These are Cowork’s manual, automatic, and no-approval modes.
  • Tray vs briefcase: The tray usually represents Projects; the briefcase represents Customize or Capabilities.

If your layout differs, check the icon’s nearby label before clicking; Anthropic moves controls and rolls out features by plan. You can also compare Claude with other AI apps for iPhone and iPad.

  • I replaced ChatGPT with Claude. Here’s what actually changed
  • Here’s the full list of Claude.ai commands you can use right now

title.rendered: How to get Pollo Sprite in Fortnite: Locations, ability, and more

content.rendered:
Fortnite has a long tradition of collaborating with esports professionals and content creators associated with the game. Streamers such as Ninja and competitive gaming prodigies such as Bugha have received their own themed Fortnite cosmetics. The outcome of one such collaboration is the Pollo Sprite that arrived in the ongoing Runners season.

First introduced in mid-July, Pollo Sprite is inspired by the namesake Fortnite pro, who currently boasts a total of four FNCS championships. The Mythic-rarity sprite offers the player and his nearby squad members a slow rate of shield regeneration upon eliminating an opponent.

Below, you can check out the places across Fortnite Island where streamers have previously found the Pollo Sprite. Moreover, you can also learn about alternative ways of obtaining the sprite.

Ways to find the Pollo Sprite in Fortnite

At the onset, the Pollo Sprite was extremely hard to come by because it was exclusively owned by the Fortnite pro it was based on, Pollo. So, in the initial days, you could only grab one by eliminating Pollo and taking the namesake sprite from him.

The fact that it required you to play on the same server as the popular streamer and join during the same time he went online further added to the challenge and to the sprite’s rarity. During that period, it was only in the possession of Pollo and of those players who got it through either eliminating him or from those who had previously eliminated him.

However, since those early days, the Pollo Sprite has started appearing in chests as well, just like other sprites. As a consequence, its ownership has increasingly grown over the past few weeks.

1. Hunting for chests

The most straightforward way of acquiring the Pollo Sprite is through chests scattered across the unranked Battle Royale map. These can be found in a wide spectrum of locations, ranging from unlockable vaults, underground spaces, and random spots in the map. In particular, the Sprite Chests and special variants of the Sprite Chest are likely to provide the Pollo Sprite.

2. Take it from another player

Fortnite is a highly competitive game, so it’s no surprise that sportsmanship is basically non-existent in it. Because of this, it’s fair game for you to simply take the Pollo Sprite from an opponent.

Before the match begins, on Spawn Island, you can check if any player is sporting the Pollo Sprite on his back. If you happen to find one such player, take note of his appearance and try to jump off from the Battle Bus at the same time as him at the start of the match. Next, you simply have to chase the target down and eliminate him in order to take the desired sprite.

3. Index it from a friend

A more friendly version of obtaining the Pollo Sprite from another player involves joining a match with that player with the sole purpose of quickly borrowing the sprite. To find players willing to help, you may visit Fortnite’s official Discord server and check out the “sprite-runners-network” channel.

This method happens over the course of two matches, the first one in which you take the sprite and extract it and the second one in which you return it to the original owner.

Wrapping up

Fortnite’s collabs with esports personalities and streamers have often taken the form of cosmetic bundles appearing in the Item Shop. However, the partnership with Pollo, which has given birth to one of the more exciting sprites in the game instead, is something unique in the same category.

Hopefully, this particular instance sets a precedent and future collabs with similar faces also produce items that go beyond the visual aspect—a change that would be welcome by both Fortnite players and the celeb’s own fans.

title.rendered: Apple’s annual India sales reportedly cross $10 billion for the first time

content.rendered:
Apple reportedly generated more than $10 billion in annual sales in India for the first time. Bloomberg reports that revenue grew at a double-digit rate in the 12 months through March 2026, up from about $9 billion a year earlier.

The figure comes from a person familiar with the private information, not Apple. The source said iPhones accounted for a significant majority of sales, while demand for iPads and MacBooks also increased. Apple did not respond to Bloomberg’s request for comment.

This is not Apple Store revenue alone

The $10 billion covers Apple’s overall sales in India. It should not be read as revenue generated only by the company’s physical stores.

Apple also does not publish India as a separate sales region. Its latest filing for the period ending in March groups the country into Rest of Asia Pacific, so the reported figure cannot be checked against a public India breakdown.

Apple’s retail footprint has tripled since 2023

Apple opened its first two stores in India in Mumbai and New Delhi in 2023. Its Noida and second Mumbai expansion helped take the physical store count to six by February 2026, with locations across Mumbai, New Delhi, Bengaluru, Pune, and Noida.

That expansion gives more customers a direct way to try devices, trade in older products, get financing, and receive support. It also gives Apple more control over how its products are sold in one of its fastest-growing markets.

India is also a major iPhone manufacturing base, but that is a separate part of the story. The reported $10 billion measures sales in India, not the value of Indian-made iPhones exported to other countries.

title.rendered: Apple CarPlay is coming to pontoon boats in 2027

content.rendered:
Marine navigation app Savvy Navvy has launched support for Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and select 2027 Crest and Balise pontoons will put it at the helm.

What boaters get on the display

Savvy Navvy calls this the first marine navigation app to run on CarPlay and Android Auto. It brings 2D and 3D marine charts, smart routing, saved markers, shallow-zone data, nearby boat traffic, and live location sharing to a compatible helm display.

Boaters can plan a route in the Savvy Navvy phone app and have it waiting on the boat display when they connect. Routes changed at the helm also appear in the app. Downloaded charts work offline, while the connection can be wired or wireless depending on the phone and display.

Which boats will include it?

MasterCraft Boat Holdings says the app will be standard on all new 2027 Balise pontoons and Crest Conquest and Caribbean models.

Eligible Crest boats include one month of Savvy Navvy Premium, while Balise buyers get a year. After that, using Savvy Navvy in CarPlay requires Premium or Premium+ in the US and the Elite plan elsewhere.

Existing boat owners do not need a new pontoon. Savvy Navvy says the app is available worldwide now and works with compatible aftermarket marine head units.

This is not CarPlay Ultra

Despite the factory integration, this is not CarPlay Ultra, which can span multiple screens and work with a vehicle’s gauges and controls. Savvy Navvy runs as a third-party navigation app in standard CarPlay, a category Apple already supports on its Dashboard. The regular platform is also gaining new navigation and voice-control tools in iOS 27.

In other words, Apple is not replacing the boat’s instruments. CarPlay is giving boaters a familiar screen for marine routes, music, and calls at the helm.

title.rendered: Telegram says extortionist tricked Apple into briefly removing its app

content.rendered:
Telegram CEO Pavel Durov says a “takedown extortionist” planted AI-modified child sexual abuse material (CSAM) in a public group, triggering the app’s brief removal from Apple’s App Store. Telegram returned about 40 minutes later after the content was removed and the account was banned.

How the alleged takedown attack worked

According to Durov, the attacker edited an old message in an active group to add the illegal material. He claims the backdated edit kept it out of view for most members, reducing the chance that someone would report it to Telegram first.

Durov says these attackers demand money from group owners and use automated accounts to plant prohibited content in communities that refuse to pay. They then report the material directly to Apple in an attempt to get the community, or in this case the entire app, removed.

Telegram’s explanation has not been independently confirmed. Apple has also not publicly addressed the extortion claim or Durov’s allegation that it removed the app before contacting Telegram.

Apple confirmed the CSAM violation, not the extortion claim

Apple told Reuters that its review found content violating its strict rules against CSAM. The company said it restored Telegram after the developer “promptly removed the content and banned the user who posted it.”

The interruption affected new downloads, not people who already had Telegram installed. The app is available again on the U.S. App Store.

Apple’s App Review Guidelines make developers responsible for moderating user-generated content. Apps must filter objectionable posts, provide reporting and blocking tools, and respond to complaints. Apple can temporarily remove an app until it demonstrates better compliance, while serious or repeated violations can lead to immediate removal.

This is not Apple’s only recent App Store enforcement test. It previously warned Grok to fix deepfake violations or risk removal, while a separate policy update gave App Review more room to remove stale copycat apps. Those cases involve different rules, but all raise the question of how consistently Apple explains and applies removal decisions.

The flagged content was removed quickly. But if Durov’s account is accurate, the episode also shows how a malicious user could weaponize App Store enforcement against a much larger service. For iPhone users, the immediate issue is over: Telegram is back, and installed copies kept working throughout the removal.

How to redeem Ninja Time codes

The code box is tucked inside the Extra Menu rather than shown on the main screen.

  1. Open Ninja Time on Roblox.
  2. Click Menu in the upper-left corner.
  3. Select Extra Menu.
  4. Open Codes or the Twitter-bird icon.
  5. Paste a working code into the box.
  6. Press Enter to claim the spins.

Why a Ninja Time code may not work

  • It expired: Update and compensation codes can disappear without warning.
  • The punctuation is wrong: Keep every ! and ? exactly as shown.
  • The capitalization is wrong: Copy and paste the code instead of retyping it.
  • You already used it: Each code usually works once per Roblox account.
  • Your server is old: Leave and join a fresh server after a new code drops.

Do not add spaces before or after a code. Also note that DelayDelayDelay and DelayDelayDelay! are two different strings.

Where to find more Ninja Time codes

New codes usually arrive with patches, new missions, reworks, delays, or shutdown fixes. The best official places to watch are:

  • Ninja Time Discord

  • Boss Studio x Luxinn Games on Roblox

The Discord is normally the fastest source, but bookmarking this page saves you from digging through announcements and testing old strings.

title.rendered: Dragon Soul codes (August 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Dragon Soul codes on August 04, 2026

Dragon Soul’s open-world fights get tougher as you chase stronger forms, better stats, and valuable wishes. The working codes below give you free Dragon Balls, an Exemplary Orb, extra Zenkai Soul luck, and an XP boost, saving you some of the grind. These rewards help whether you are starting fresh or returning for a new update. Redeem them as soon as possible, since Dragon Soul codes can expire without warning.

All working Dragon Soul codes

  • newqolupdate: 7 Dragon Balls (NEW)
  • apementor: 7 Dragon Balls
  • devluck: Double Zenkai Soul luck
  • qolupdate: 7 Dragon Balls (Discord verification required)
  • dragonballs: 5 Dragon Balls
  • exclusive: 7 Dragon Balls and 1 Exemplary Orb (Discord verification required)
  • dragonsoul: 30% XP boost for 3 hours

Start with newqolupdate, since it is the newest freebie. Then copy the remaining codes exactly to avoid losing a reward to a small typo.

Expired Dragon Soul codes

webrokeraids, webrokeraidss, valentine, GODREWORK, events, dragon, ultrassj3, 200k, Beast, JAPAN, NEWYEARS2025, 300klikes, shatteredorbs, souls, dragonsoulswhen, 200klikes, 180klikes, 160klikes, 125KLikes, 100KLIKES, RADRIBBON, boostspack, HalloweenHype, DragonBallsComingSoon, Twitch/fuegowave, GARO, shrimpgame, 100milplays, 20kLIKES, 8KLIKES, XPGRIND

These older strings no longer unlock rewards. They are worth keeping around only to avoid mistaking an expired code for a typo.

How to redeem Dragon Soul codes

On PC, the code box sits inside the main menu.

  1. Open Dragon Soul on Roblox.
  2. Press M to open the menu.
  3. Select Codes on the right.
  4. Paste a working code into the Enter Code Here box.
  5. Select Redeem Code to collect the reward.

Why a Dragon Soul code may not work

  • It expired: Event and update codes can disappear without warning.
  • The capitalization changed: Copy the code instead of retyping it.
  • You already used it: Each code normally works once per Roblox account.
  • Your server is old: Leave the game and join a fresh server after a new code drops.
  • Your account is not verified: qolupdate and exclusive may require verification through the official Discord.

Remove any spaces before or after the code. If it still fails in a fresh server, treat it as expired rather than retrying it repeatedly.

Where to find more Dragon Soul codes

New codes usually arrive with updates, milestones, seasonal events, or shutdown fixes. The useful official pages to watch are:

  • Dragon Soul Discord
  • Novaly Studios on X
  • Dragon Soul (DS) on Roblox

title.rendered: Why turning off Windows Game Mode improved my gaming performance

content.rendered:
I always assumed Windows Game Mode was helping my games. After all, Microsoft designed it specifically to improve gaming by prioritizing system resources for the game you’re playing. It sounded like a feature you should simply leave enabled and forget about.

However, after noticing occasional stutters and inconsistent frame pacing in a few games, I decided to check whether Game Mode is really helping my PC in any way. The results surprised me because disabling Game Mode did not increase my average FPS greatly but helped to make the gameplay smoother and improved CPU behavior in some titles.

Here are the best Windows settings for gaming performance, and whether you should turn off Game Mode.

What Windows Game Mode actually does

Windows Game Mode is a built-in feature designed to improve gaming performance by giving your game higher priority over most background processes. When enabled, Windows attempts to allocate more CPU resources to the active game while reducing interruptions from unnecessary system tasks.

Some of the things Game Mode is designed to do include:

  • Prioritize the running game over background applications.
  • Reduce Windows Update activity while gaming.
  • Adjust CPU scheduling to favor game processes.
  • Work alongside gaming-related Windows features such as Xbox Game Bar.

That sounds great on paper, but there’s one misconception I see quite often: many people assume Game Mode automatically increases FPS. That’s not how it works.

Here’s a quick comparison.

On modern gaming PCs with powerful processors, Windows already manages resources very efficiently. In those cases, the additional scheduling changes introduced by Game Mode may have little effect. In some situations, I even faced minor performance inconsistencies.

Why I decided to turn it off

The reason I started experimenting was that some of my games simply didn’t feel as smooth as they should have.

Average FPS looked perfectly fine, but I noticed:

  • Random micro-stutters during gameplay
  • Frame pacing that felt inconsistent
  • Occasional FPS drops in CPU-heavy scenes
  • CPU utilization fluctuating more than expected
  • GPU usage not always staying close to full load

Since these symptoms usually point toward CPU scheduling or background resource management, Game Mode became one of the first settings I decided to test.

My gaming results before and after

Rather than relying on a single benchmark run, I tested multiple games several times using identical graphics settings and gameplay scenarios. 

My system for the test included i7-13700H + RTX 4060 Laptop + 16GB DDR5 + Windows 11 25H2. I also closed unnecessary background applications before every test to eliminate as many variables as possible.

Average FPS

The average FPS difference between Game Mode enabled and disabled wasn’t dramatic.

Depending on the game, the difference was only a few frames per second. In some titles, there was almost no measurable change at all. However, higher FPS doesn’t always mean smoother gameplay.

1% Low FPS

Where I noticed more meaningful differences was in the 1% low FPS numbers. These represent the slowest 1% of rendered frames and are a much better indicator of gameplay smoothness than average FPS.

Without Game Mode, frame drops happened less often in many games, and as a result, there was smoother camera motion and less hitching.

If you’re troubleshooting gaming performance, I recommend paying close attention to 1% lows instead of focusing only on the highest FPS number.

Frame Time consistency

Frame times became the greatest improvement that I have noticed.

With Game Mode enabled, I occasionally noticed small spikes during CPU-intensive moments. These didn’t always reduce average FPS enough to show up in benchmarks, but I could feel them while playing.

Disabling Game Mode made the frame time graph more consistent and smooth, with fewer sudden spikes. That translated into gameplay that simply felt smoother, even when the FPS counter barely changed.

CPU and GPU behavior

I also monitored CPU and GPU utilization during testing.

On my system:

  • CPU boost clocks stayed more consistent.
  • CPU scheduling appeared more stable.
  • GPU utilization remained closer to full load in certain games.
  • Overall system responsiveness felt slightly better during gameplay.

Again, these improvements weren’t huge, but together they made the gaming experience noticeably more enjoyable.

Why turning off Game Mode helped

After comparing all the benchmarks, I don’t think Game Mode itself is a “bad” feature. Instead, I believe my particular hardware simply didn’t benefit from the way Windows was prioritizing workloads.

  • My PC didn’t need extra scheduling: With plenty of CPU cores available and few apps running in the background, Windows already had enough resources to manage games efficiently. In that situation, Game Mode didn’t have much optimization to perform.
  • Better CPU boost behavior: Disabling Game Mode allowed the processor to boost more consistently during CPU-heavy scenes. Even small improvements in boost behavior can reduce frame-time spikes.
  • Fewer scheduling conflicts: NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel graphics already include their own optimizations for games. Enabling additional scheduling through Windows Game Mode may occasionally create unnecessary overlap rather than improving performance.
  • Frame pacing improved more than FPS: Smooth gameplay matters more than chasing the highest FPS number. Average FPS barely changed, but improved frame pacing made games feel noticeably better to play.

When you should keep Game Mode enabled

Even though switching off Game Mode helped me more with my PC, I would not advise anyone to disable it for good. There is a reason why Microsoft introduced Windows Game Mode, and in many cases, it may really boost your gaming experience.

Here are a few situations where I’d keep it enabled.

1. You have an older or budget gaming PC

If your PC has a quad-core processor or limited system resources, background tasks can have a much bigger impact on gaming performance. Game Mode can help by giving the game higher priority and reducing interruptions from other processes.

2. You frequently multitask while gaming

Many gamers leave several apps open while playing, including:

  • Discord
  • Google Chrome
  • Spotify
  • Steam downloads
  • RGB control software
  • Game launchers

In these situations, Game Mode may help prevent those background applications from competing with your game for CPU resources.

3. You record or stream gameplay

If you regularly use OBS Studio, Xbox Game Bar, or other recording software, it’s worth testing Game Mode before turning it off. In some cases, priority of the game process over others may help minimize performance issues.

4. You’re using a gaming laptop

Gaming laptops often have stricter power and thermal limits than desktop PCs. Because of that, Windows’ built-in optimizations can sometimes produce better results than manual tweaking.

Quick Recommendation

The key takeaway is simple: don’t assume one setting is universally better. Spend 15–20 minutes benchmarking both options to see which performs best on your system.

Other Windows settings I tested to improve my gaming experience

Together with Game Mode, I tried a couple of other Windows settings. Some made a noticeable difference, while others had little to no impact on my system.

1. Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS)

HAGS allows the graphics card to manage its own memory scheduling instead of relying entirely on the CPU.

On my PC, I didn’t notice a significant FPS increase, but some newer games felt slightly more responsive with it enabled. Since results vary depending on your GPU and drivers, it’s another setting worth benchmarking.

2. Xbox Game Bar

A lot of people confuse Xbox Game Bar with Game Mode, but they’re separate features.

Game Bar provides overlays for screenshots, performance monitoring, and game recording. If you never use these features, disabling the overlay may reduce background activity slightly, although I didn’t notice a major performance gain.

3. Fullscreen optimizations

Windows’ Fullscreen Optimizations can improve compatibility in some games but may introduce input lag or inconsistent performance in others.

For older DirectX games, disabling this setting occasionally resulted in smoother gameplay. For newer titles, I generally left it enabled.

4. Variable Refresh Rate (VRR)

If your monitor supports G-Sync, FreeSync, or Windows Variable Refresh Rate, make sure it’s enabled.

Unlike Game Mode, VRR can have a much bigger impact on perceived smoothness by reducing screen tearing and minimizing stutter when frame rates fluctuate.

5. High Performance Power Plan

I also compared the Balanced and High Performance power plans.

The differences were very minor on modern processors, because the Windows Balanced power plan allows aggressive CPU boosts during gaming, and switching to another power plan doesn’t result in FPS gain on my machine.

6. Memory Integrity (Core Isolation)

Memory Integrity is a Windows security feature that can slightly reduce performance in CPU-bound workloads.

Disabling it may improve gaming performance on some systems, but I recommend doing so only if you understand the security trade-offs. For most gamers, the difference is small enough that leaving it enabled is the safer choice.

7. Background Startup Apps

This ended up having a bigger impact than I expected.

Turning off unnecessary applications, like RGB controllers, cloud synchronization, and unused launchers, made background CPU activity lower.

In fact, cleaning up startup apps made a more noticeable difference than changing several Windows gaming settings.

Final verdict: Should you turn off Windows Game Mode?

After testing Game Mode across multiple gaming sessions, I came away with one conclusion: there isn’t a universal answer.

Disabling Game Mode on my PC did not result in any great increase in average FPS, although there were definite improvements in frame pacing and occasional stutters, making gameplay smoother. I found these to be more important changes compared to the gain in a few frames per second.

It does not mean, however, that Game Mode is not effective at all. In case you have an older processor, have a budget laptop, or play while multitasking, keeping Game Mode turned on will give you better performance. Windows designed the feature to prioritize games under heavier system loads, and it can do that effectively in the right scenarios.

My advice is simple:

  1. Benchmark your favorite games with Game Mode enabled.
  2. Turn it off and repeat the exact same tests.
  3. Compare more than just average FPS—look at 1% lows, frame times, CPU utilization, and overall smoothness.
  4. Keep whichever setting delivers the best real-world experience on your hardware.

Gaming performance isn’t determined by a single Windows feature. Drivers, power settings, background applications, game optimizations, and your hardware all play important roles.

In my case, switching Game Mode off was definitely worth the effort as it gave me smoother gameplay. This may work for you too, but maybe keeping it on will bring even better results. It all depends on your PC configuration and how you use it. The most effective thing is to test the difference for yourself.

  • Ava is a die-hard Apple aficionado and loves testing the latest tech gadgets.

title.rendered: How to get the John Wick Sprite in Fortnite

content.rendered:
John Wick has been a big part of the Fortnite Runners season. Not only has the dashing action hero been featured in the Battle Pass, but now he has also been added as a new sprite in Epic’s online multiplayer game.

Since their makeover this season, sprites have become extremely popular in the Fortnite community. During this period, a few special sprites based on notable real-life and fictional personalities were also introduced, such as Vini Jr Sprite and Batman Sprite.

The most recent addition to this list of unique sprites is the John Wick Sprite inspired by the protagonist of the namesake film franchise. Below, you can learn more about this sprite and how you can get your hands on it.

John Wick Sprite availability and usage

Unlike the other sprites introduced so far, the John Wick Sprite is exclusive to Fortnite Reload. However, once get your hands on it and extract it, you can also bring it with you on your escapades in other Fortnite modes, such as Battle Royale.

As an extension of the above possibility, you may also come across the John Wick Sprite in modes other than Reload if someone who extracted it earlier chooses to equip the sprite and bring it to a different mode.

You can put the John Wick Sprite to good use in situations where you are surrounded by enemies. That’s because equipping it grants you the ability to locate nearby opponents by knocking down any one of them.

What this perk helps you do is, when you are in a place crawling with opponents, you can knock one down and immediately mark where the others are lurking. This can prove very beneficial in strategizing your next move or planning a tight escape.

How to find and extract John Wick Sprite in Fortnite

The John Wick Sprite is a Mythic-tier sprite, viz., it’s among the rarest sprites in the highly popular live-service game. It can be obtained from chests in Fortnite Reload or picked up as loot from other players in modes such as the standard Battle Royale and Zero Build. As a result, the primary way to get hold of the sprite involves ransacking through the Reload map and unlocking as many chests as you can.

However, it’s worth noting that extracting the sprite might prove to be more challenging than obtaining it. And that’s down to there being no Extraction Sites in Reload’s map. So, you would have to go back to chest-hunting and look to get a Portable Extractor instead, which, being Legendary-tier, is very hard to come by.

Fortunately, there is another considerably easier way of getting the Portable Extractor. This involves purchasing it from a Mending Machine in exchange for 50 Gold. Moreover, obviously, you can also extract the John Wick Sprite by simply winning the match.

Wrapping up

By restricting the John Wick Sprite’s spawn locations to Fortnite Reload’s map, Epic Games has certainly tried to mix things up a bit. This not only gives players a refreshing change in their quest for sprites but also offers a strong incentive to dive into the recently Simpsons-ified Reload mode.

Overall, it’s a smart move by Fortnite devs to leverage the popularity of sprites and of the Springfield map—whose previous iteration was available in Battle Royale instead—in order to make Reload more appealing and boost its engagement.

FAQs

Which Fortnite modes can I use John Wick Sprite in?

You can use John Wick Sprite in Reload, standard Battle Royale, and Zero Build.

Are there any other John Wick items in Fortnite right now?

Yes, besides the John Wick Sprite, there are the John Wick (Pen & Ink) skin, the Simpsons-style John Wick skin, a 9mm Baba Yaga pistol, and John Wick’s dog sidekick.

How to unlock the John Wick skin in Fortnite?

For the John Wick (Pen & Ink) skin, you will have to purchase the Battle Pass and progress to Level 84. On the other hand, the Simpsons-style John Wick skin requires you to own the Battle Pass as well as complete all four of the “John Wick (The Simpsons) Contracts” quests.

  • How to get the Sir Wyvern sidekick in Fortnite

acceptedAnswer.text: Among the Bleach Wave 1 additions were skins inspired by Orihime Inoue, Rukia Kuchiki, Ichigo Kurosaki, and Uryu Ishida, as well as themed pickaxes, back blings, emotes, wraps, and decals.

mainEntity.name: Which other popular anime has collaborated with Fortnite before?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apart from Bleach, Dragon Ball, Naruto, Jujutsu Kaisen, Attack on Titan, and My Hero Academia have previously been featured in Fortnite.

mainEntity.name: Which Fortnite modes can I use John Wick Sprite in?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can use John Wick Sprite in Reload, standard Battle Royale, and Zero Build.

mainEntity.name: Are there any other John Wick items in Fortnite right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, besides the John Wick Sprite, there are the John Wick (Pen & Ink) skin, the Simpsons-style John Wick skin, a 9mm Baba Yaga pistol, and John Wick's dog sidekick.

mainEntity.name: How to unlock the John Wick skin in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: For the John Wick (Pen & Ink) skin, you will have to purchase the Battle Pass and progress to Level 84. On the other hand, the Simpsons-style John Wick skin requires you to own the Battle Pass as well as complete all four of the "John Wick (The Simpsons) Contracts" quests.

title.rendered: How to get the Lil Tecca skin in Fortnite

content.rendered:
After being revealed as the Fortnite Festival headline singer earlier this week, Lil Tecca has now been introduced in the Item Shop. In addition to getting a skin inspired by the American rapper, the in-game store has also received emotes, a jam track, and other themed cosmetics.

Fortnite players have ample time to get their hands on these items as they are available until August 28, 2026, by 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET. In particular, the Lil Tecca skin can be bought for 1,800 V-Bucks and comes bundled with the Dopamine Blades pickaxe and back bling. Check out the guide below to see each step involved in claiming the Lil Tecca Fortnite skin from the Shop.

Steps to get the Lil Tecca skin in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, navigate to the Shop tab.
  2. Scroll down to the Lil Tecca section and select the Lil Tecca skin.
  3. Press and hold the Purchase button to confirm your decision.

Besides purchasing the skin on its own, you may also claim the same by purchasing the Lil Tecca Bundle, worth 2,600 V-Bucks. This pack includes all Lil Tecca cosmetics, except the 500lbs jam track, that are up for grabs in the store right now. In total, the bundle purchase saves you as much as 2,100 V-Bucks.

Other Lil Tecca cosmetics in Fortnite

1. Dopamine Blades (pickaxe and back bling)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: Lil Tecca Bundle, Lil Tecca skin

2. Lil World Mic (pickaxe and back bling)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available in: Lil Tecca Bundle

3. Ransom (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available in: Lil Tecca Bundle

4. Dark Thoughts (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available in: Lil Tecca Bundle

5. Ransom (jam track)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available in: Lil Tecca Bundle

6. Dark Thoughts (jam track)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available in: Lil Tecca Bundle

7. 500lbs (jam track)

Price: 500 V-Bucks

8. Tecca Bars (wrap)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available in: Lil Tecca Bundle

Wrapping up

Over the years, Fortnite has presented several popular and rising singers as avatars within its world that players can take control of. To this end, the Fortnite Festival mode has ensured that there is a regular stream of such celeb cosmetics in Epic’s online multiplayer title.

In 2026 itself, we have seen music industry stars such as Lisa, Chappell Roan, and Laufey land in the game, thanks to them headlining Fortnite Festival. With Lil Tecca being the latest one on board, the music-centric mode continues to thrive and, with it, so does the game’s musician skins catalog.

FAQs

Has Lil Tecca been added to Fortnite before?

No. This is Lil Tecca’s first appearance of any kind in the game.

How many rappers have previously been introduced as skins in Fortnite?

Previously, rappers including Eminem, Travis Scott, Snoop Dogg, Ice Spice, Juice WRLD, and more have been added as skins to the game.

Which popular singers are there in Fortnite’s skin catalog?

Apart from rappers, other popular singers in Fortnite include Ariana Grande, Billie Eilish, Sabrina Carpenter, The Weeknd, and Lady Gaga, among others.

In case you missed:

  • How to get Spider-Man Brand New Day skins in Fortnite
  • How to get MCU Iron Man and Captain America skins in Fortnite
  • How to get the Mongraal skin in Fortnite
  • How to get Squid Game skins in Fortnite

title.rendered: WhatsApp beta for Mac adds daily and weekly update options

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is giving some Mac beta testers a choice between getting new builds as often as daily or using a steadier weekly release. The new controls apply only to the beta app, and availability is still limited.

According to WABetaInfo, recent WhatsApp beta builds for Mac are gaining an App updates section in Settings. It shows the installed version, includes a Check for updates button, and lets testers switch update tracks without reinstalling the app.

Daily builds or a steadier weekly release

The setting offers two choices with different trade-offs:

  • Latest version: Can receive daily builds with new fixes and stability improvements. It may also get features before the weekly build, but work-in-progress bugs are more likely.
  • Stable weekly version: Bundles changes into one update per week, usually before the weekend, for a more predictable experience.

Both tracks are meant to receive the same core features. The difference is how quickly a tester gets them and how much beta instability they are willing to accept.

This does not affect the stable Mac app

WABetaInfo says WhatsApp discontinued its Mac beta through TestFlight earlier this year. Testers now download beta builds directly from WhatsApp’s servers, and the new controls bring update choices into the app, much like other non-App Store Mac apps.

The regular WhatsApp app for Mac remains separate from this beta track. If you use the public version, these daily and weekly choices do not change how your app updates.

The new section is rolling out gradually to some Mac beta testers. WhatsApp has not announced when every tester will get it or whether similar controls will come to the stable app.

excerpt.rendered: WhatsApp is rolling out daily and weekly update options to some Mac beta testers, but the controls are not yet available in the stable app for everyone.
