title.rendered: How to restart Fortnite on PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo Consoles

content.rendered:
Being a live-service game, Fortnite gets an endless cascade of updates, big and small. And, with each update, new changes and occasionally new issues are also introduced in the game. In such a scenario, a quick restart can resolve general bugs and similar problems until a patch is rolled out by the devs.

While on PC, restarting Fortnite is as simple as clicking on the profile icon and selecting Quit Game; each console handles the process a little differently. To know how to restart the game on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2 consoles, check out the steps below.

Steps to restart Fortnite on Consoles

Restart Fortnite on PS5

  1. In Fortnite, press and hold the PS button to open the quick menu.
  2. Highlight Fortnite and press the Options button.
  3. Close the game by pressing the X button.
  4. Go to the home screen, go to Fortnite and press the X button to start it again.

Restart Fortnite on Xbox Series X/S

  1. In Fortnite, press the Xbox button to open the guide.
  2. Highlight Fortnite from the list on the left side of the screen and press the menu button.
  3. Select “Quit” by pressing the A button.
  4. From the home screen or library, go to Fortnite and press the A button to launch it again.

Restart Fortnite on Nintendo Switch and Switch 2

  1. With Fortnite running, press the Home button on the right Joy-Con.
  2. Navigate to the Fortnite icon on the home screen and press the X button on the right Joy-Con.
  3. Select “Close“.
  4. After it closes, highlight Fortnite again and press the A button to restart it.

Wrapping up

From in-game network hiccups to graphical bugs, doing a quick restart generally fixes a lot of such common issues in Fortnite. As a result, it is the first thing that you should try upon encountering any error or bug in the popular online game.

However, certain other issues in Fortnite, such as the invalid Pak error, may require more digging before they get fixed. If you’re facing that exact problem, be sure to check out our guide on how to fix the “Pak is invalid” error.

FAQs

Which in-game issues can restarting Fortnite help with?

By restarting Fortnite, you can get rid of any temporary glitches, performance lag, and even network issues, besides a host of other general problems.

How to restart Fortnite if it freezes on console?

If your system is completely frozen and you can’t even access the menus, then do a hard restart of the console itself by pressing and holding the power button for at least 15 seconds. This method works more or less the same way across all three consoles.

Which is the best way to restart Fortnite on console?

For quickly fixing common issues, restarting the game via the console menu is the best option.

mainEntity.name: Why is Windows reserving 8GB of RAM?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common causes include integrated graphics reserving system memory, incorrect BIOS settings, the Maximum memory option being enabled in MSConfig, outdated firmware, or improperly installed RAM. If the BIOS detects all installed memory, Windows configuration is usually the next place to investigate.

mainEntity.name: Is hardware reserved RAM bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Every Windows PC reserves a small amount of memory for hardware components. It only becomes a concern when several gigabytes are unavailable without an obvious reason.

mainEntity.name: Can I disable hardware reserved memory?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't completely disable it because some hardware requires reserved memory to function. However, if an unusually large amount is reserved due to a configuration issue, correcting the underlying problem can make that memory available again.

mainEntity.name: Does upgrading RAM fix this?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you're genuinely running out of memory. If Windows is reserving large portions of your installed RAM because of BIOS or configuration issues, installing additional memory won't help much. It's better to identify why the existing memory isn't fully usable first.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Private Instagram accounts aren't included in this AI image feature. Only eligible public content can be used.

mainEntity.name: Does opting out delete existing AI images?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Opting out helps prevent future AI image generation using your eligible public content, but it doesn't automatically remove images that may already have been generated.

mainEntity.name: Will people know if I use their photos?

mainEntity.name: Does Windows 11 predictive text work with any keyboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Text suggestions work with most standard physical keyboards connected to a Windows 11 PC, whether they're wired, wireless, or built into a laptop. The feature depends on Windows itself rather than the keyboard hardware.

mainEntity.name: Does predictive text work offline?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Once enabled, Text Suggestions and Autocorrect work without an internet connection because they're built into Windows 11.

mainEntity.name: Why don't text suggestions appear?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your system is completely frozen and you can't even access the menus, then do a hard restart of the console itself by pressing and holding the power button for at least 15 seconds. This method works more or less the same way across all three consoles.

title.rendered: iOS 27 makes it easier to share iPhone albums with Android

content.rendered:
I love using Shared Albums on my iPhone, especially after trips, vacations, or family events. Everyone can upload their photos, react to pictures, and keep the entire collection organized in one place. The only problem was that this convenience usually disappeared as soon as someone in the group used an Android phone.

The usual solution was sending photos over WhatsApp or uploading them somewhere else, which meant another app, another link, and another place to manage everyone’s photos.

With iOS 27, Apple is finally making Shared Albums feel useful outside its own ecosystem. I shared one with my Android friends, and they could not only view the album but also add their own photos without needing an iPhone.

Keep reading to learn how it works.

What are Shared Albums on iPhone?

Shared Albums is an iCloud Photos feature that lets you create separate albums and share them with other people. Instead of sending individual photos through messaging apps or creating separate folders elsewhere, you can keep everything inside the Photos app.

A Shared Album is much more than a regular folder in the Photos app. Regular albums only help you organize photos already in your library, but a Shared Album creates a space that other people can access.

Depending on the permissions you choose, people in the album can view photos, add their own pictures, and interact with the shared collection. It works more like a shared photo space where everyone can contribute instead of a folder that only exists on your iPhone.

The best part is that people don’t need to use the same device as you. iPhone users can access Shared Albums directly from the Photos app, while Android users can open them through an iCloud link in their browser.

Before creating one, make sure Shared Albums are enabled on your iPhone:

  1. Open the Settings app, scroll down and tap iCloud.
  2. Here, select Photos under Saved to iCloud.
  3. Now, tap Shared Albums under Sharing.
  4. Next, toggle on Shared Albums.

Once enabled, you can create and share albums directly from the Photos app.

How to create a Shared Album on iPhone

After enabling Shared Albums, you can create one directly from the Photos app.

  1. Open the Photos app and select the photos and videos you want to add to the Shared Album.
  2. Tap the Share button.
  3. Here, tap the Add to Shared Album button.
  4. Now, select an existing Shared Album or tap the + (Add) button to create a new Shared Album.
  5. Give your Shared Album a name.
  6. Next, choose one of the Sharing Options:
    • People You Choose
    • Anyone with the Link.
  7. Tap Done.

How to share an iPhone shared album with Android users

Since Android doesn’t have Apple’s Photos app, Shared Albums are accessed through an iCloud web link. Here’s how:

  1. Open the Shared Album.
  2. Here, tap the Share button.
  3. Next, share the invite link with the Android user via your preferred app.

What Android users see when they open the shared album

Opening a Shared Album link on Android feels similar to viewing any other web photo gallery. The album opens in the browser through iCloud Photos, showing the album name along with the photos and videos you have shared.

Your friends don’t need to install another app or create an Apple Account just to see the album. Everything works through the browser, which makes it much easier for groups where everyone uses different devices.

While the experience isn’t identical to using the Photos app on an iPhone, it removes the biggest limitation. Everyone can access the same photo collection from one place.

How to manage a Shared Album

You can update the Shared Album by adding more photos, changing permissions, or controlling who can contribute.

By default, participants can add their own photos and videos to the Shared Album. However, the person who created the album can change this later and set participants to view-only access.

One feature I really appreciate is that Android users aren’t limited to viewing photos. They can also upload their own pictures directly through the iCloud web interface.

Here’s how:

  1. Open the shared iCloud album link in a browser.
  2. Tap the Add Photos button at the top.
  3. Enter your email address and tap Continue.
  4. Enter the six-digit verification code sent to your email.
  5. Select and upload the photos you want to add.

After verification, Android users can contribute their own photos to the same album without needing an iPhone or Apple Account.

This is especially useful for trips and events because everyone can add their pictures to one shared place instead of creating multiple photo dumps across different apps.

Final thoughts

Apple’s sharing features have always worked best when everyone uses Apple devices, but that’s rarely how real groups work. Friends, families, and coworkers often have a mix of iPhones and Android phones.

iOS 27 reduces that friction by keeping the experience simple for both sides. iPhone users can manage everything from the Photos app, while Android users can still view and contribute through the web.

After using it with Android friends, it finally feels like sharing memories doesn’t have to depend on everyone owning the same phone.

mainEntity.name: Why is Windows reserving 8GB of RAM?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common causes include integrated graphics reserving system memory, incorrect BIOS settings, the Maximum memory option being enabled in MSConfig, outdated firmware, or improperly installed RAM. If the BIOS detects all installed memory, Windows configuration is usually the next place to investigate.

mainEntity.name: Is hardware reserved RAM bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Every Windows PC reserves a small amount of memory for hardware components. It only becomes a concern when several gigabytes are unavailable without an obvious reason.

mainEntity.name: Can I disable hardware reserved memory?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't completely disable it because some hardware requires reserved memory to function. However, if an unusually large amount is reserved due to a configuration issue, correcting the underlying problem can make that memory available again.

mainEntity.name: Does upgrading RAM fix this?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you're genuinely running out of memory. If Windows is reserving large portions of your installed RAM because of BIOS or configuration issues, installing additional memory won't help much. It's better to identify why the existing memory isn't fully usable first.

mainEntity.name: Does predictive text work offline?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Once enabled, Text Suggestions and Autocorrect work without an internet connection because they're built into Windows 11.

mainEntity.name: Why don't text suggestions appear?

acceptedAnswer.text: There are several possible reasons. Text suggestions isn't enabled in Settings > Time & Language > Typing, or the application you're using may not support Windows' predictive typing. Also, the feature is not available in all languages.

mainEntity.name: Which in-game issues can restarting Fortnite help with?

acceptedAnswer.text: By restarting Fortnite, you can get rid of any temporary glitches, performance lag, and even network issues, besides a host of other general problems.

mainEntity.name: How to restart Fortnite if it freezes on console?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your system is completely frozen and you can't even access the menus, then do a hard restart of the console itself by pressing and holding the power button for at least 15 seconds. This method works more or less the same way across all three consoles.

mainEntity.name: Which is the best way to restart Fortnite on console?

acceptedAnswer.text: For quickly fixing common issues, restarting the game via the console menu is the best option.

His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: Apple Health adds menopause tracking in iOS 27. Here’s how it works

content.rendered:
Apple’s Health app has long been a convenient place to keep important health information, but Cycle Tracking has mostly focused on periods, fertility, and pregnancy. With iOS 27, Apple is expanding it to support another important stage of life: perimenopause and menopause.

The new menopause tracking feature helps you record symptoms, understand changes in your cycle, and see health trends over time. It also provides personalized insights within the Health app, so you don’t have to switch between multiple apps or rely on memory to track changes over time.

Here’s how you can set up and use menopause tracking on your iPhone.

How to set up menopause tracking in Apple Health

  1. Open the Health app and head to the Browse tab.
  2. Here, locate and tap Cycle Tracking.
  3. Scroll down and tap Menopause Stages.
  4. Now, tap the + (add) button in the top right corner to add your menopause stage.
  5. Next, select the option that describes you and follow the onscreen instructions to complete the menopause tracking setup.

Once it’s enabled, the Health app will organize your symptoms, cycle information, and related health data in one place.

What can you track with menopause tracking?

Every person’s menopause journey is different, which is why tracking a variety of symptoms can provide more meaningful insights over time.

With menopause tracking in the Health app, you can record symptoms and changes such as:

  • Hot flashes
  • Night sweats
  • Sleep changes
  • Mood changes
  • Cycle irregularities
  • Other menopause-related symptoms

Over time, these entries can help you spot patterns that may be difficult to remember otherwise. For example, you might notice whether certain symptoms happen more often during specific periods or alongside changes in sleep and lifestyle.

How to log menopause symptoms on iPhone

Once menopause tracking is set up, adding symptoms only takes a few seconds.

  1. Open the Health app → Browse → Cycle Tracking.
  2. Now, tap Symptoms under Log or changes you want to record.
  3. Next, select the symptom.
  4. Tap Done to save your entry.

Over time, the Health app analyzes your symptom history alongside your cycle data to identify patterns that might otherwise be difficult to notice.

How menopause insights and notifications work

In iOS 27, the Health app can also provide insights when your cycle history shows changes that may be related to perimenopause.

These insights are designed to highlight possible trends in your data. While they aren’t intended to replace medical advice, they can provide useful information to discuss with your healthcare provider.

To enable notifications:

  1. Open the Health app → Browse → Cycle Tracking.
  2. Tap Options.
  3. Turn on the necessary toggles.

Is your menopause data private?

Health information is extremely personal, and menopause-related data is no exception. Apple encrypts Health data and gives you full control over which apps can access it.

You can review permissions anytime by going to:

  • Settings → Privacy & Security → Health

From there, you can see which apps have access to your Health data and remove permissions if needed.

Tips for getting better menopause insights

The Health app becomes more useful when it has consistent information to work with. A few habits can improve your long-term tracking:

  • Log symptoms as close to when they happen as possible.
  • Track sleep patterns along with menopause symptoms.
  • Add information regularly instead of waiting weeks.
  • Review your trends every month to notice changes.

Small updates over time can create a much clearer picture than trying to remember everything later.

Do you need an Apple Watch for menopause tracking?

Menopause tracking works directly inside the Health app on your iPhone, so an Apple Watch is not required.

However, if you already use an Apple Watch, it can add more health information like sleep trends and other wellness metrics. Combining these additional metrics with menopause tracking can provide a more complete picture of your overall health.

Final thoughts

Menopause tracking in iOS 27 is a meaningful expansion of Apple’s Cycle Tracking feature. Instead of focusing only on reproductive health, the Health app now supports another major health transition with symptom logging, insights, and long-term trends.

Like most health tracking features, menopause tracking becomes increasingly valuable the longer you use it. Logging symptoms consistently can help you better understand long-term changes and keep everything organized in one place.

Do you think menopause tracking makes the Health app more useful? Share your opinion in the comments below.

mainEntity.name: Why is Windows reserving 8GB of RAM?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common causes include integrated graphics reserving system memory, incorrect BIOS settings, the Maximum memory option being enabled in MSConfig, outdated firmware, or improperly installed RAM. If the BIOS detects all installed memory, Windows configuration is usually the next place to investigate.

mainEntity.name: Is hardware reserved RAM bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Every Windows PC reserves a small amount of memory for hardware components. It only becomes a concern when several gigabytes are unavailable without an obvious reason.

mainEntity.name: Can I disable hardware reserved memory?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't completely disable it because some hardware requires reserved memory to function. However, if an unusually large amount is reserved due to a configuration issue, correcting the underlying problem can make that memory available again.

mainEntity.name: Does upgrading RAM fix this?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you're genuinely running out of memory. If Windows is reserving large portions of your installed RAM because of BIOS or configuration issues, installing additional memory won't help much. It's better to identify why the existing memory isn't fully usable first.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: WhatsApp is testing birthday notifications for contacts on Android

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is working on a new feature that will notify users when one of their contacts has a birthday. The feature was spotted by WABetaInfo in the latest WhatsApp beta for Android 2.26.27.3 update on the Google Play Store.

The upcoming feature builds on the birth year information WhatsApp started collecting earlier for regulatory requirements. However, WhatsApp is now exploring ways to use birthday-related information beyond age verification by adding reminders inside the app.

A new birthday section is in development

According to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is creating a dedicated section where users will be able to see upcoming birthdays shared by their contacts. The section is expected to work as a central place for birthday reminders instead of relying on a separate calendar app or remembering dates manually.

When a contact’s birthday arrives, WhatsApp will show a notification inside the app. It could be useful for people who mainly rely on WhatsApp for staying in touch and often end up sending birthday messages there anyway.

However, birthday reminders will depend on whether contacts have shared their date of birth with WhatsApp. If someone has not provided birthday information, the app will not be able to show a reminder for that contact.

Privacy controls could arrive before launch

At the moment, WhatsApp has not added dedicated privacy settings for birthday sharing. Users currently do not have controls to decide whether their birthday should be visible to contacts or only used by WhatsApp for age verification.

Since the feature is still in early development, WhatsApp could add more privacy options before making it publicly available.

The birthday notification feature is currently being developed for a future Android update and is not available to beta testers yet. WhatsApp has not announced when the feature will roll out, but more details are expected as development continues.

Would you use birthday reminders inside WhatsApp? Let us know in the comments below.

excerpt.rendered: WhatsApp is developing birthday notifications for Android, allowing users to receive in-app reminders when their contacts celebrate a birthday.

mainEntity.name: Why is Windows reserving 8GB of RAM?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common causes include integrated graphics reserving system memory, incorrect BIOS settings, the Maximum memory option being enabled in MSConfig, outdated firmware, or improperly installed RAM. If the BIOS detects all installed memory, Windows configuration is usually the next place to investigate.

mainEntity.name: Is hardware reserved RAM bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Every Windows PC reserves a small amount of memory for hardware components. It only becomes a concern when several gigabytes are unavailable without an obvious reason.

mainEntity.name: Can I disable hardware reserved memory?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't completely disable it because some hardware requires reserved memory to function. However, if an unusually large amount is reserved due to a configuration issue, correcting the underlying problem can make that memory available again.

mainEntity.name: Does upgrading RAM fix this?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you're genuinely running out of memory. If Windows is reserving large portions of your installed RAM because of BIOS or configuration issues, installing additional memory won't help much. It's better to identify why the existing memory isn't fully usable first.

mainEntity.name: Does Windows 11 predictive text work with any keyboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Text suggestions work with most standard physical keyboards connected to a Windows 11 PC, whether they're wired, wireless, or built into a laptop. The feature depends on Windows itself rather than the keyboard hardware.

mainEntity.name: Does predictive text work offline?

title.rendered: Apple TV scores 89 nominations at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards

content.rendered:
The Academy of Television Arts & Sciences has announced the nominees for the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards, and Apple TV has picked up 89 nominations this year.

Among the highlights, Michael J. Fox received a nomination for his guest appearance in Shrinking, while Widow’s Bay earned the most nominations of any new series this year.

The nominations follow a strong performance last year, when Apple received a record 81 nominations and won 25 awards. The Studio led the way with 13 wins, including Best Comedy Series, while Severance picked up eight awards, including acting wins for Britt Lower and Tramell Tillman.

Apple TV shows nominated across major categories

Apple’s original lineup is represented across several of the biggest Emmy categories this year.

Pluribus, Slow Horses, and Your Friends and Neighbors are nominated for Outstanding Drama Series, while Margo’s Got Money Troubles, Shrinking, and Murderbot received nominations for Outstanding Comedy Series.

Apple also received multiple acting nominations.

Gary Oldman earned a Lead Actor in a Drama Series nomination for Slow Horses, while Rhea Seehorn was nominated for Lead Actress in a Drama Series for Pluribus.

In comedy categories, Elle Fanning received a Lead Actress nomination for Margo’s Got Money Troubles, while Jason Segel earned a Lead Actor nomination for Shrinking. Harrison Ford, Jessica Williams, Michael Urie, and Michael J. Fox were also recognized for their performances in Apple TV shows.

More Apple originals receive recognition

Beyond the main drama and comedy categories, Palm Royale received nominations for choreography, production design, costumes, and hairstyling, while Foundation, Monarch: Legacy of Monsters, and Prehistoric Planet: Ice Age landed nominations for visual effects.

Apple’s nonfiction lineup was also recognized, with Mr. Scorsese and The Reluctant Traveler With Eugene Levy receiving nominations.

Apple also received nominations outside Apple TV, with Apple Music’s Super Bowl LX Halftime Show starring Bad Bunny nominated in multiple variety categories. Apple’s commercials A Critter Carol and I’m Not Remarkable were also nominated for Outstanding Commercial.

The 78th Primetime Emmy Awards will air live on September 14 at 8 p.m. ET / 5 p.m. PT, with Mariska Hargitay hosting the ceremony.

Which Apple TV show do you think deserves the biggest Emmy win this year? Let us know in the comments below.

mainEntity.name: Why is Windows reserving 8GB of RAM?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common causes include integrated graphics reserving system memory, incorrect BIOS settings, the Maximum memory option being enabled in MSConfig, outdated firmware, or improperly installed RAM. If the BIOS detects all installed memory, Windows configuration is usually the next place to investigate.

mainEntity.name: Is hardware reserved RAM bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Every Windows PC reserves a small amount of memory for hardware components. It only becomes a concern when several gigabytes are unavailable without an obvious reason.

mainEntity.name: Can I disable hardware reserved memory?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't completely disable it because some hardware requires reserved memory to function. However, if an unusually large amount is reserved due to a configuration issue, correcting the underlying problem can make that memory available again.

mainEntity.name: Does upgrading RAM fix this?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you're genuinely running out of memory. If Windows is reserving large portions of your installed RAM because of BIOS or configuration issues, installing additional memory won't help much. It's better to identify why the existing memory isn't fully usable first.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: OpenAI launches GPT-Live to make ChatGPT Voice feel more human

content.rendered:
OpenAI has introduced GPT-Live, a new generation of voice models that now power ChatGPT Voice. The company says the update is meant to make talking with ChatGPT feel closer to a real conversation, with less stiff turn-taking and smarter answers when a question needs deeper work.

GPT-Live is rolling out globally now across iOS, Android, and ChatGPT.com. Tap the Voice button, and the new experience should start showing up as it reaches your account.

ChatGPT can listen while it talks

Older ChatGPT voice modes still worked more like a walkie-talkie. You spoke, then waited. Advanced Voice Mode improved the sound and speed, but it still relied on discrete turns and often jumped in after a short pause.

GPT-Live is full duplex. It can listen and speak at the same time, and OpenAI says the model can decide many times per second whether to keep listening, speak, pause, interrupt, or call a tool.

In practice, that means you can cut in with a question, stop to think, or ask ChatGPT to slow down. OpenAI also says the model will acknowledge you with short phrases like “mhmm” or “got it,” and it is better at waiting when you pause instead of treating silence as your turn ending. Background noise handling is improved too, so nearby chatter or traffic is less likely to throw it off.

OpenAI remastered ChatGPT’s nine built-in voices for GPT-Live. The system is still limited to those predefined voices, with safeguards against imitating a real person’s voice.

Smarter answers without freezing the chat

OpenAI calls GPT-Live its smartest voice model yet. When a request needs web search, deeper reasoning, or more complex work, GPT-Live can hand that job off in the background and keep the conversation going. At launch, that background model is GPT-5.5.

Users can also pick how hard ChatGPT should think: Instant for speed, or Medium and High when a slower, more careful answer is worth the wait.

Voice chats can now show rich visual cards while you talk, including weather, stocks, sports, and maps. Search, memory, images, and file uploads still work in voice conversations.

OpenAI also says the continuous design helps with live translation and longer, more fluid back-and-forth. In its own head-to-head tests, GPT-Live was preferred over Advanced Voice Mode for conversational flow, and it scored better on several reasoning and search-style evaluations.

Free and paid users get different models

OpenAI is shipping two versions:

  • GPT-Live-1: default for ChatGPT Go, Plus, and Pro
  • GPT-Live-1 mini: default for Free users

Both are part of the global rollout. Developers and businesses can join a waitlist for API access, which OpenAI says is coming soon.

What is still missing

At launch, GPT-Live does not support voice with video or screen sharing in ChatGPT. OpenAI says those features are coming. Until then, users can still reach legacy Standard and Advanced Voice Mode where those options are available.

OpenAI also notes that GPT-Live is optimized for some of ChatGPT’s most popular languages. In others, users may hear a non-native accent or weaker fluency while language quality improves.

Why this matters

More than 150 million people already talk to ChatGPT each week through Voice and Dictation, according to OpenAI. A full-duplex model is a clear step toward the kind of always-on voice assistant people expect on phones, in the car, and eventually on hardware. That fits the broader direction of a voice-first OpenAI device that leans more on conversation than screens.

The company is also treating voice safety as its own problem, not just a text model with speakers. GPT-Live includes voice-specific safeguards, support flows for sensitive conversations, and teen protections. Parents can control whether a teen can use ChatGPT Voice through parental controls, and linked parents may get alerts in higher-risk self-harm situations.

For most people, the test is simple: open ChatGPT, start a voice chat, and see whether interruptions, pauses, and follow-up questions feel less robotic. If GPT-Live sticks the landing, ChatGPT Voice stops being a novelty mode and becomes a normal way to get real work done out loud.

mainEntity.name: Why is Windows reserving 8GB of RAM?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common causes include integrated graphics reserving system memory, incorrect BIOS settings, the Maximum memory option being enabled in MSConfig, outdated firmware, or improperly installed RAM. If the BIOS detects all installed memory, Windows configuration is usually the next place to investigate.

mainEntity.name: Is hardware reserved RAM bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Every Windows PC reserves a small amount of memory for hardware components. It only becomes a concern when several gigabytes are unavailable without an obvious reason.

mainEntity.name: Can I disable hardware reserved memory?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't completely disable it because some hardware requires reserved memory to function. However, if an unusually large amount is reserved due to a configuration issue, correcting the underlying problem can make that memory available again.

mainEntity.name: Does upgrading RAM fix this?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you're genuinely running out of memory. If Windows is reserving large portions of your installed RAM because of BIOS or configuration issues, installing additional memory won't help much. It's better to identify why the existing memory isn't fully usable first.

mainEntity.name: Which in-game issues can restarting Fortnite help with?

acceptedAnswer.text: By restarting Fortnite, you can get rid of any temporary glitches, performance lag, and even network issues, besides a host of other general problems.

mainEntity.name: How to restart Fortnite if it freezes on console?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your system is completely frozen and you can't even access the menus, then do a hard restart of the console itself by pressing and holding the power button for at least 15 seconds. This method works more or less the same way across all three consoles.

title.rendered: I finally found the best power bank for My Galaxy S26 Ultra after testing many

content.rendered:
The Galaxy S26 Ultra comes with a big battery, but in real life, it’s surprisingly easy to drain it. Between using Galaxy AI features, editing videos, navigating with GPS, and playing games, I often found myself reaching for a charger before the day was over. The worst part? Although there was a power bank on me at all times, it charged rather slowly and did not help much.

So I decided to test several popular power banks, from Samsung’s own model to budget picks and high-capacity monsters. Some promised 45W charging but never activated Samsung’s Super Fast Charging. Others were too bulky to carry around. One even got uncomfortably warm during extended use.

After all that testing, I finally found the ones worth buying. Here is the best power bank I ended up choosing, why it stood out from the rest, and the other options that are still a good alternative if you own a Galaxy S26 Ultra.

Why finding the right power bank for the Galaxy S26 Ultra was hard

The Galaxy S26 Ultra is surprisingly picky about charging accessories. I learned that the hard way.

Many brands advertise “fast charging,” but unless a power bank supports USB Power Delivery (PD), you’re not getting Samsung’s fastest charging speeds. On paper, two 45W power banks can look identical. In reality, one charges the phone noticeably faster than the other.

Then there’s portability. A huge battery sounds great, but having to carry an extra pound every day is not desirable. Add poor build quality, inefficient battery conversion, no temperature control, or slow recharging, and what looked like a bargain quickly becomes frustrating.

After trying several models, I stopped chasing the biggest numbers on the box and started focusing on real-world performance.

What I needed in a power bank

Before buying another S26 Ultra charger, I made a checklist.

  • Support Samsung’s fast charging protocol
  • At least 20,000mAh for travel
  • Compact enough to carry daily
  • Solid build quality
  • Multiple USB-C ports
  • Good efficiency without excessive heat

I also preferred a built-in USB-C cable and a battery display instead of four tiny LEDs. Once you’ve used a percentage display, it’s hard to go back.

Top 6 power banks for Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra

1. Samsung Galaxy Magnetic Wireless 5,000mAh Battery Pack: The official choice

If you already own several Samsung accessories, this feels like the safest purchase. Everything just works without any setup.

It offers super-fast wired and Qi2-certified wireless charging for the S26 Ultra. During my testing, the magnetic alignment made quick top-ups incredibly convenient. The cutout design fits the back of the S26 Ultra well. Note that you need a magnetic case to attach it.

Moreover, the built-in kickstand was also surprisingly useful during video calls. The downside is simple: 5,000mAh isn’t enough for heavy users. If I’m traveling all day, I usually want more capacity. Also, using it outdoors generated quite a bit of heat.

Pros

  • Official Samsung accessory
  • Excellent build quality
  • Magnetic wireless charging
  • Built-in kickstand

Cons

  • Expensive for its capacity
  • Only 5,000mAh
  • Wireless charging is slower than wired

My verdict: I’d buy this only if you already live inside Samsung’s ecosystem. It’s beautifully made, but you’re paying extra for convenience rather than raw battery life.

Check out on Amazon

2. UGREEN Nexode 20,000mAh Power Bank: Best value for money

If I could recommend only one power bank to most iPhone and Galaxy S26 Ultra owners, this would probably be it.

UGREEN Nexode consistently delivered fast 45W wired charging thanks to Super Fast Charging 2.0 protocol. The Intelligent Temperature Monitoring and multi-protection system kept the battery cool under load. I also appreciated having enough capacity to recharge my phone multiple times or juice up three devices simultaneously.

The integrated braided USB-C cable helps to charge my S26 Ultra anytime, anywhere, even if I forget the cable. Also, the battery pack has a flexible cable loop that doubles as a handy carrying strap. Overall, UGREEN Nexode hits the sweet spot between size, performance, and price.

Pros

  • Excellent super-fast charging support
  • Great battery efficiency
  • Premium construction
  • Multiple USB-C ports

Cons

  • Slightly heavier than slim models
  • Takes time to recharge fully

My verdict: This became my everyday power bank. It’s best for most Galaxy S26 Ultra owners looking for the best overall value.

Check out on Amazon

3. INIU 20,000mAh small power bank: Best budget option

Budget power banks usually make compromises somewhere. Surprisingly, this one doesn’t make many.

I didn’t expect much before testing the INIU portable charger, but it consistently outperformed several competitors. Despite packing a 20,000mAh battery, it’s compact enough to fit comfortably in my pocket. It’s made possible due to the industry-first high-density TinyCell battery. You can get super-fast 45W charging with the USB-C PD and QC support.

Additionally, the power bank supports charging up to three devices at once, making it useful when I’m carrying my S26 Ultra accessories or traveling with someone else. The built-in flashlight will help out in emergencies. Therefore, it’s proof that you don’t have to spend a fortune to get dependable charging.

Pros

  • Affordable
  • Lightweight and compact for its capacity
  • Built-in digital display and flashlight
  • 3-Year INIU Care

Cons

  • The cable loop comes undone sometimes
  • Display isn’t as premium

My verdict: The biggest surprise of my testing. It performs far better than its price suggests. Ideal for students, casual users, and anyone shopping on a tight budget.

Check out on Amazon

4. LISEN Ultra Slim 10000mAh Power Bank: Best for carrying around

Some days, I don’t need maximum capacity. I just need something that disappears into my pocket. That’s exactly what the LISEN delivers.

It’s slim enough (only 0.5-inch thick) to carry everywhere without feeling like an extra brick. The built-in USB-C cable eliminates the need to carry an extra charging cable. For office days or short trips, it became the charger I reached for most often. The aluminum unibody looks sleek and premium.

Although it’s thin, LISEN has integrated an NTC AI-driven temperature and current control chip. My only concern is that the power bank provides up to 22.5W fast charging, which charges my S26 Ultra slower than the others.

Pros

  • Extremely slim and lightweight
  • CCC-certified and TSA-approved
  • Travel-friendly
  • Good everyday charging

Cons

  • Only one USB-C port
  • Not ideal for super fast charging

My verdict: Not the most powerful, but easily the one I carried the most every day. If you’re a daily commuter or minimalist, go for it.

Check out on Amazon

5. SHARGE HyperTower 25,000mAh Portable Charger: Best high-capacity power bank for S26 Ultra

This thing is a beast. On a two-day trip, I brought only this battery in my travel accessories kit. It easily handled charging my phone, earbuds, smartwatch, and even a tablet at once. What impressed me most is that it supports 170W total output and up to 100W from a single USB-C port. So, the power bank can fast-charge a laptop as well.

The built-in USB-C cables are incredibly convenient because I don’t have to pack extra charging cables, and the smart display lets me monitor the remaining battery, charging speed, and power output in real time. And worry not, it’s airline-friendly. However, the power bank is larger and pricier than others, so I would recommend it for power users only.

Pros

  • Massive battery capacity
  • Charges 4 devices together
  • Great travel companion
  • Excellent for power users 

Cons

  • Heavy
  • Takes longer to recharge

My verdict: Massive, heavy, and completely worth it for travelers, photographers, and content creators. 

Check out on Amazon

6. TORRAS PolarCircle Qi2.2 Wireless Charger: Best wireless power bank for Galaxy S26 Ultra

Normally, I like wired charging since it’s faster, but this particular magnetic S26 Ultra accessory actually changed my mind. The magnetic alignment snaps the phone into position instantly. There’s no fumbling with cables, especially when I’m working at my desk or watching videos.

The standout feature is the built-in cooling system. Most wireless chargers got noticeably warm in longer charging tests, especially during navigation, gaming, or video streaming. The PolarCircle’s active cooling keeps temperatures under control, helping it maintain consistent charging speeds instead of slowing down because of heat.

The 25W Qi2.2 wireless charging, thanks to the included Torras IceNano 45W plug, also feels much quicker than traditional wireless chargers. Another feature I ended up using more than expected is the 360-degree rotating stand. It lets me switch between portrait and landscape mode while charging.

Pros

  • Strong magnetic attachment
  • Premium quality with compact design
  • Built-in fan to prevent overheating
  • Included 45W adapter for reliable performance

Cons

  • Lower efficiency than wired charging
  • Premium price

My verdict: The most convenient charger I tested. It won’t replace wired charging, but it’s the one I grab when working at the desk. 

Check out on Amazon

Things I learned after testing so many power banks

Testing these power banks taught me a few lessons I wish I’d known from the beginning.

  • Advertised wattage means very little if the charger doesn’t properly support Samsung’s charging protocol.
  • Bigger isn’t always better. A 25,000mAh power bank is fantastic for travel but overkill for everyday commuting.
  • I have also discovered that the charging cable plays an important role. Switching to a quality USB-C cable noticeably improved charging consistency.

Finally, buying from trusted brands saved me the most frustration. Cheap no-name power banks often exaggerated their capacity and delivered inconsistent charging speeds.

Is a 10,000mAh or 20,000mAh power bank better for the Galaxy S26 Ultra?

It depends on how you use your phone.

  • If you’re mostly commuting, working in an office, or need emergency backup, a 10,000mAh power bank is easier to carry and usually provides around one to two full charges.
  • If you travel frequently, shoot lots of photos, use Galaxy AI features heavily, or game on your phone, I believe 20,000 mAh is the perfect balance. It allows for several charges without being overly large.

Personally, after testing both sizes, I’d choose a quality 20,000mAh model every time. The extra capacity gives me peace of mind without adding too much weight.

Final verdict

After weeks of testing, one thing became obvious: not every “45W” power bank is actually designed for Samsung phones.

  • If I wanted the best overall recommendation, I’d buy the UGREEN Nexode 20,000mAh again without hesitation. It strikes the perfect balance between charging speed, reliability, portability, and price.
  • If you prefer official Samsung accessories, the Samsung Magnetic Battery Pack is a great companion for everyday use. Budget shoppers should look at INIU, while travelers who never want battery anxiety will appreciate the HyperTower 25,000mAh.

The right power bank isn’t the one with the biggest number on the box—it’s the one you’ll actually carry every day. For me, that’s what finally made the difference. Which power bank will you choose? Let me know in the comments below.

FAQs

Does the Galaxy S26 Ultra support 45W charging from a power bank?

Yes, but only if the power bank supports USB Power Delivery in a wired connection. Without Super Fast charging support, your phone may charge at a slower speed even if the power bank advertises 45W output.

Which cable should I use for the fastest charging?

Use a high-quality USB-C to USB-C cable rated for 5A and 100W charging. Samsung’s official cable or a certified cable from trusted brands like UGREEN, Anker, or INIU will help ensure you get the fastest and most stable charging speeds.

mainEntity.name: Why is Windows reserving 8GB of RAM?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common causes include integrated graphics reserving system memory, incorrect BIOS settings, the Maximum memory option being enabled in MSConfig, outdated firmware, or improperly installed RAM. If the BIOS detects all installed memory, Windows configuration is usually the next place to investigate.

mainEntity.name: Is hardware reserved RAM bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Every Windows PC reserves a small amount of memory for hardware components. It only becomes a concern when several gigabytes are unavailable without an obvious reason.

mainEntity.name: Can I disable hardware reserved memory?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't completely disable it because some hardware requires reserved memory to function. However, if an unusually large amount is reserved due to a configuration issue, correcting the underlying problem can make that memory available again.

mainEntity.name: Does upgrading RAM fix this?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you're genuinely running out of memory. If Windows is reserving large portions of your installed RAM because of BIOS or configuration issues, installing additional memory won't help much. It's better to identify why the existing memory isn't fully usable first.

title.rendered: How to customize your Roblox avatar

content.rendered:
Your Roblox avatar does not have to stay on the default look. The Avatar Editor lets you change clothes, accessories, hair, skin tone, body style, faces, animations, and emotes, while the Roblox Marketplace gives you more free and paid items to add.

You only need a logged-in Roblox account. Some items are free, while others cost Robux, so check the price before you hit Buy or Get.

How to customize your Roblox avatar on the website

Use the web version if you want the clearest layout and easier Marketplace browsing.

  1. Go to Roblox and log in.
  2. Select Avatar from the left menu. You can also open the Avatar Editor directly after logging in.
  3. Open a category such as Clothing, Accessories, Body, or Animations.
  4. Click an item to equip it. Click it again to remove it.
  5. Wait for the avatar preview to update.

Roblox saves avatar changes automatically. If the preview changes, your avatar has been updated; you do not need a separate Save button for normal item changes.

How to customize your Roblox avatar on mobile

The mobile app uses a tighter layout, but the idea is the same.

  1. Open the Roblox app.
  2. Select Avatar.
  3. Tap Customize.
  4. Choose the item type you want to change.
  5. Tap an item to equip or remove it.

If you do not see the same labels, update the Roblox app or use the website. Roblox sometimes moves Avatar and Marketplace controls around, but the Avatar section is still the place to edit your character.

How to get new clothes, accessories, and avatar items

If your inventory feels empty, open the Roblox Marketplace from the website or the Shop tab inside the Avatar area.

  1. Search for the item you want, such as a hoodie, hair, hat, face, bundle, or emote.
  2. Use filters to narrow results by category, creator, price, or availability.
  3. Choose Free if you do not want to spend Robux.
  4. Open the item page.
  5. Select Get for free items or Buy for paid items.
  6. Return to Avatar > Customize and equip the item from the matching category.

Be careful with off-platform links promising free Robux or rare avatar items. If you plan to spend Robux or use Roblox-related sites, read these Roblox account safety tips first.

How to change skin tone, body, and animations

Clothes change the outfit, but the Body and Animations sections change how your avatar is built and moves.

  • Skin tone: Open Body and look for Skin or Skin Tone.
  • Hair: Open Body or Accessories, depending on where Roblox places your hair items.
  • Head or face: Open Body and choose Heads or Faces if available.
  • Body shape: Look for Scale, Build, or body/bundle options inside Body.
  • Walk and idle style: Open Animations and equip the animation pack or movement style you want.
  • Emotes: Open Emotes or Animations and assign the emotes you want to use in supported experiences.

Do not overthink this part on day one. Pick a clean outfit first, then adjust body shape and animations only if the avatar still feels off.

Why your Roblox avatar is not changing

If your new look does not show up, check these common causes before buying the same item again.

  • The item is not equipped: Buying or claiming an item adds it to your inventory, but you may still need to equip it.
  • The preview has not refreshed: Switch categories, refresh the page, or restart the app.
  • The item was removed or moderated: Some items can disappear if Roblox removes them from the platform.
  • The experience overrides avatars: Some games use custom characters, force R6/R15 styles, or hide certain accessories.
  • You are using the wrong account: Check the username before changing or buying anything.
  • You do not have enough Robux: Paid items will not be added unless the purchase completes.

If an item works in the Avatar Editor but not inside one specific game, the game is probably controlling how avatars appear. Try joining a different Roblox experience to confirm.

A few quick avatar style tips

The best Roblox avatars usually have one clear idea instead of ten random accessories fighting for attention.

  • Start with one outfit theme: casual, sporty, fantasy, horror, anime, or funny.
  • Match hair, face, and accessories before buying more clothes.
  • Use free items first if you are still testing a look.
  • Avoid bulky accessories if they block your view in games.
  • Save Robux for items you will actually wear across multiple experiences.

Once your avatar is ready, you can jump back into games and claim free rewards from our Roblox game codes list if you want boosts, currency, or other in-game extras in supported experiences.

  • What it actually takes to get Verified on Roblox

mainEntity.name: Why is Windows reserving 8GB of RAM?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common causes include integrated graphics reserving system memory, incorrect BIOS settings, the Maximum memory option being enabled in MSConfig, outdated firmware, or improperly installed RAM. If the BIOS detects all installed memory, Windows configuration is usually the next place to investigate.

mainEntity.name: Is hardware reserved RAM bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Every Windows PC reserves a small amount of memory for hardware components. It only becomes a concern when several gigabytes are unavailable without an obvious reason.

mainEntity.name: Can I disable hardware reserved memory?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't completely disable it because some hardware requires reserved memory to function. However, if an unusually large amount is reserved due to a configuration issue, correcting the underlying problem can make that memory available again.

mainEntity.name: Does upgrading RAM fix this?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you're genuinely running out of memory. If Windows is reserving large portions of your installed RAM because of BIOS or configuration issues, installing additional memory won't help much. It's better to identify why the existing memory isn't fully usable first.

title.rendered: Apple just upgraded Messages in iOS 27: Here are the biggest changes

content.rendered:
Apple has announced iOS 27 with some of the long-requested features like Siri AI, Liquid Glass refinements, more system-integrated Apple Intelligence capabilities, and updates to native apps. While most of the attention has been focused on AI, Apple’s Messages app is also getting a handful of quality-of-life upgrades.

The biggest changes include one-tap suggestions, a new drawing app, faster media sharing, and improved child safety protections. While testing the iOS 27 beta, I found some additional improvements as well. Here are all the new features coming to Messages in iOS 27.

1. One-tap suggestions make conversations faster

With iOS 27, Messages is starting to understand what you’re trying to do.

Now Apple Intelligence can surface one-tap suggestions directly inside conversations. If someone asks you to remember something, Messages can suggest creating a reminder or adding a note. If a friend asks for photos from a recent trip, the app can automatically find relevant images based on people, locations, and keywords.

I recently got an invitation to an event, and an Add to Calendar suggestion popped up under the text. Additionally, based on the discussion, Messages recommends what Genmoji I would like to create.

That matters because we make plans, share information, organize trips, and manage our lives inside chat threads. Until now, every action required jumping between apps. Apple is trying to let you do the required action without leaving the chat.

2. Messages get a new drawing and image creation experience

Apple also added something unexpected: a dedicated Drawing app inside Messages. Simply tap the plus icon next to the text box and select Drawing. It shows the familiar Markup tools that allow you to draw, annotate, or doodle and send it directly.

At first glance, this feels oddly niche. But look closer, and it starts making sense. Apple is clearly preparing for a larger-screen foldable iPhone Ultra and stylus-based interaction.

Apple is also expanding image-generation capabilities through Apple Intelligence and Image Playground, making it easier to create and share AI-generated visuals across conversations.

3. Write with Siri in Messages

One standout feature is Write with Siri inside Messages. Instead of manually typing every reply, you can ask Siri to draft an entire message, proofread text, or give feedback on a message based on a simple prompt. From iOS 27 beta 2, a dedicated Write with ‌Siri‌ button appears above the keyboard.

For example, I asked Siri to write a polite message explaining that I’d be 20 minutes late for dinner. Within seconds, it generated a well-written text that sounded conversational rather than robotic. If the wording didn’t feel quite right, I could tweak it before sending. It felt much more natural than the older dictation feature.

What impressed me most was how Siri AI empowers Smart Reply suggestions to adapt more closely to your personal writing style for each recipient, making the responses more natural. In addition, Siri can now help you locate images, videos, links, addresses, phone numbers, etc. in the Messages app.

4. Continuous sending of photos and videos

This might be the most underrated upgrade in iOS 27.

Apple says Messages now supports continuous sending of photos, videos, and texts in the background. If you have just captured an image or clip, it appears in a second in the Messages media picker. No need to wait.

In addition to this, failed messages, even with media attachments, can automatically retry to deliver once connectivity is re-established. It seems like Apple has finally recognized that speed and reliability matter more than flashy effects. Honestly, it took longer than it should have.

5. Better protection for children

This is one area where Apple put a major highlight at the WWDC keynote.

For child accounts, Messages can now automatically detect and block violent or gore content shared through images and videos. That expands on Apple’s existing Communication Safety tools, which already warn children about nudity and sensitive content.

Parents are also gaining more control over who their children can contact through Messages, FaceTime, and Phone. New communication requests can require parental approval before a child connects with someone new.

The broader Screen Time overhaul in child safety features introduces additional controls, including website approvals, app category limits, and more flexible access scheduling.

6. View offloaded media

One of the most frustrating experiences in Messages happens when older photos and videos have been offloaded to save local storage. You can see the conversation, but the media feels like it has vanished, as only generic placeholders were shown.

iOS 27 addresses this problem by showing visible preview thumbnails for offloaded media so you can easily recognize them. Moreover, Search can surface those photos and videos more easily inside conversations.

It’s the kind of feature that sounds small, but users end up appreciating it every time they need to find a photo from years ago.

7. Inline replies to iPhone-to-Android RCS chats

The latest iOS 27 beta 2 adds support for inline replies in RCS conversations. This means iPhone users can now reply directly to a specific message when chatting with Android users, just like they already can in iMessage conversations.

If you’ve ever been part of a busy group chat, you’ll know how easy it is to lose track of which message someone is responding to. With inline replies, you can simply press and hold a message and choose Reply. Your response is then attached to that specific message, making the conversation much easier to follow.

This update also has another improvement for making iPhone-to-Android chats better. In iOS 27, tapaback emoji reactions appear properly on photos and videos in cross-platform conversations, instead of text descriptions.

Keep in mind that inline replies require RCS to be supported by both devices and carriers involved in the conversation.

8. Updated Genmoji

Apple is giving Genmoji a meaningful upgrade in iOS 27. You can now change individual elements and refine an existing Genmoji instead of generating a brand-new one whenever you want a small tweak. If an emoji is close but not quite right, I simply use the new Describe a change interface to create a better version.

Genmoji can even handle multi-step requests to generate more detailed emojis. For example, I could start with a smiling cat, then ask it to wear sunglasses, hold a coffee cup, and stand on a beach. The interface even suggested possible follow-up edits, making it easy to keep refining the design until it matched what I had in mind.

Apple has also improved the quality and consistency of the generated emojis. Compared to iOS 26, the results looked much closer to Apple’s native emoji set, with a polished 3D, cartoon-like appearance by default. If that style isn’t what you’re after, you can now request a different look, such as a hand-drawn illustration or a pencil sketch.

Hidden Messages features you might miss

I found several smaller changes in the iOS 27 Messages app that could end up having a surprisingly large impact:

  • Multiple tapback reactions are consolidated into fewer notifications, reducing alert overload in busy group chats.
  • You can customize or completely remove the audio button next to the text box from Settings > Apps > Messages > Show in Text Field and choose between Record Audio, Start Dictation, or None. Selecting None prevents you from sending accidental recordings.
  • Search can now find conversations using phone numbers or saved nicknames. So, you don’t need to remember the exact contact name.
  • Large chats with extensive history and attachments now load and scroll more smoothly.
  • Messages, read receipts, reactions, and attachments sync faster and more reliably across all your Apple devices to improve continuity.

Collectively, all these features make the Messages app feel more polished than it has in years.

Which iPhones support the new Messages features?

The good news is that iOS 27 supports iPhones going back to the iPhone 11 and includes iPhone SE 2nd gen and later. That means you can access the Drawing app, hide the audio button, get consolidated tapback notifications, and other performance updates after installing iOS 27 beta.

However, the one-tap suggestions and personalized Smart Replies rely on Apple Intelligence. It will work on iPhone 15 Pro and later lineup models with Siri and the device language set to English as of now.

In other words, everyone gets the update, but not everyone gets the full experience.

Messages are finally catching up to WhatsApp and Telegram!

For the first time in a while, I think Apple is asking the right question. Instead of asking, “What new feature can we add?” Apple seems to be focusing on “What makes messaging annoying?”

The answers are obvious: failed uploads, too many notifications, hard-to-find media, repetitive actions, and safety concerns. iOS 27 tackles all of those.

Do Messages suddenly leapfrog WhatsApp and Telegram? Not yet. Telegram still dominates with its power-user features. WhatsApp remains the global messaging giant. Signal still owns the privacy conversation. But Apple no longer looks like it’s standing still. And that’s the biggest change of all.

Which iOS 27 feature are you most excited about? Let us know in the comments below!

mainEntity.name: Why is Windows reserving 8GB of RAM?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common causes include integrated graphics reserving system memory, incorrect BIOS settings, the Maximum memory option being enabled in MSConfig, outdated firmware, or improperly installed RAM. If the BIOS detects all installed memory, Windows configuration is usually the next place to investigate.

mainEntity.name: Is hardware reserved RAM bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Every Windows PC reserves a small amount of memory for hardware components. It only becomes a concern when several gigabytes are unavailable without an obvious reason.

mainEntity.name: Can I disable hardware reserved memory?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't completely disable it because some hardware requires reserved memory to function. However, if an unusually large amount is reserved due to a configuration issue, correcting the underlying problem can make that memory available again.

mainEntity.name: Does upgrading RAM fix this?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you're genuinely running out of memory. If Windows is reserving large portions of your installed RAM because of BIOS or configuration issues, installing additional memory won't help much. It's better to identify why the existing memory isn't fully usable first.

title.rendered: This hidden iOS 27 Photos app feature lets you export slideshows as videos

content.rendered:
Apple spent plenty of time talking about AI features in the WWDC keynote, but the update I ended up using first wasn’t powered by Apple Intelligence at all. It was a surprisingly useful upgrade hiding inside the Photos app.

Apple has quietly transformed the old slideshow feature into something people will actually use. Instead of creating a slideshow that’s only meant for viewing, iOS 27 now lets you customize it, add music, and export it as a proper video in the Photos app. Here’s how to save a slideshow as a video on an iPhone.

Apple finally offers a slideshow maker in the iOS 27 Photos app

One of the most surprising additions I found in iOS 27 is something Apple users have wanted for years—a proper slideshow maker built directly into the Photos app. It sounds small, but after trying it, I realized it removes the need for third-party apps for creating quick memory videos.

Previously, the Photos app could play selected images and clips as a temporary slideshow, but there was almost no creative control or a built-in way to save them as a video. If I wanted to make something worth sharing with friends or family, I had to switch to editing apps like CapCut, Canva, or iMovie. With iOS 27, Apple finally closes that gap.

And here are the things you can now do:

  • Create slideshows from selected photos and videos
  • Adjust transition style between slides and playback duration
  • Add background music from Apple’s curated library
  • Preview everything before exporting
  • Save the finished slideshow as a video directly into your Photos library

The best part is that everything happens inside the Photos app. There won’t be any need to use some special slideshow maker or editor. So now I can easily turn travel photos, family moments, or event highlights into a polished video in just a few taps.

How to export a slideshow as a video in iOS 27

I tested the feature using several travel photos and videos, and the entire process took less than a minute.

  1. Open the Photos app, tap Select, and choose the images or videos you want in your slideshow.
  2. After selecting your files, tap the three-dot button in the top-right corner.
  3. From the menu, choose Start Slideshow. Immediately, Photos generates a full-screen slideshow.
  4. Tap the screen and a large Customize button appears below the slideshow. Inside it, I found options for,
    • Transition & Duration: Change the transition style between slides and set the duration per photo to adjust the total length. Once done, tap the checkmark.
    • Music: Select Choose Song and browse curated soundtrack suggestions organized into categories. If you don’t want music, keep it as Off.
    • Loop: Enable to keep the slideshow repeating.
  5. Once you are happy with the slideshow, tap the three-dot button > Share.
  6. It will open the Share Sheet. Scroll and tap Save Video or send it directly via AirDrop, Mail, WhatsApp, etc. You can tap Options to change orientation and aspect ratio.

It renders the slideshow into a movie file and automatically saves it back into your Photos library. You can edit the video later or upload it to your social media.

Tip: While testing the feature, I came across an alert that I can’t save/share Memories that contain Apple Music songs. To choose a new soundtrack, tap Edit Music and select a song from the Soundtracks section. They are not DRM-protected.

Save a slideshow as a video on Mac

If you want to create a slideshow on your Mac, worry not; the steps are kind of similar.

  1. Open the Photos app on your Mac and go to your Library or any album.
  2. Select the photos you want to include. Hold the Command (⌘) key to pick multiple images, or press Command + A to select everything in the current view.
  3. From the menu bar, click File and select Play Slideshow.
  4. Select Customize to personalize your slideshow. Here, you can:
    • Choose transition effects. Set how long each photo stays on screen. Add background music.
  5. Once you’re happy with the slideshow, click File and select Export > Export Slideshow Video from the menu bar.
  6. Give the video a name, choose where to save it, adjust the orientation or aspect ratio if necessary, and click Save.

The Photos app will export your slideshow as an MOV video file. You can watch it on QuickTime Player, share it via AirDrop, upload it to cloud storage, or edit it further in a video editor if needed.

It’s not iMovie, and that’s exactly why I like it

Some people will probably compare this feature to iMovie. I don’t think they should.

Apple clearly isn’t trying to replace a video editor here. There are no timelines, layers, text animations, or trimming individual slides.

Instead, this feels designed for moments when you simply want to tell a story with photos without spending twenty minutes editing. That’s exactly why I think it works.

Most people don’t need professional tools every time they return from vacation or attend a birthday party. They just want something they can share.

Things I noticed during testing

After spending some time with the feature, a few details stood out.

  • The process seemed extremely fast. From picking the photos to getting the final video exported took no more than a minute. For casual users, that’s probably the biggest advantage.
  • The music selection is better than expected. Apple includes plenty of built-in soundtrack suggestions, so you don’t have to hunt through your own music library.
  • Export quality looks clean. The saved video looked sharp, and the transitions were smooth without noticeable quality loss.
  • It works well for product showcases. I tested it using product photos instead of vacation pictures, and it actually worked surprisingly well.

Small businesses could easily create quick product previews for WhatsApp Status, Instagram Stories, or Facebook without opening a dedicated editing app.

Who will get the most value?

This feature isn’t just for family photo albums.

I can see it being useful for:

  • Parents sharing birthday memories
  • Travelers creating quick vacation recaps
  • Students making event highlights
  • Small businesses showcasing products
  • Content creators posting simple photo montages
  • Anyone who wants a polished video without learning video editing

If your goal is speed rather than creative control, this feature hits the sweet spot.

A few limitations

The Photos app slideshow maker is not perfect yet.

During testing, I noticed there are still some limitations.

  • You can’t rearrange individual slides from the slideshow editor.
  • Text overlays aren’t available.
  • There are also no special effects or manual animation tools
  • Editing options remain intentionally minimal.

If you need cinematic edits or social media effects, apps like iMovie or Final Cut Pro still make more sense.

Final thoughts

Sometimes the best iOS features aren’t the ones Apple spends twenty minutes demonstrating during a keynote. This slideshow exporter is a perfect example. It takes a feature that has existed for years, fixes its biggest limitation, and makes it genuinely useful.

Will it replace professional video editors? Absolutely not. Will it save millions of iPhone users from downloading another editing app just to turn a handful of photos into a shareable video? I think it will.

If you’re updating to iOS 27, don’t overlook the Photos app. Hidden behind a tiny three-dot menu is one of the most practical upgrades Apple has added this year.

More to explore:

  • I tried iOS 27’s Call Context feature. It found my booking code during a call
  • All the new Safari features in iOS 27
  • iOS 27 Shortcuts app features

mainEntity.name: Why is Windows reserving 8GB of RAM?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common causes include integrated graphics reserving system memory, incorrect BIOS settings, the Maximum memory option being enabled in MSConfig, outdated firmware, or improperly installed RAM. If the BIOS detects all installed memory, Windows configuration is usually the next place to investigate.

mainEntity.name: Is hardware reserved RAM bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Every Windows PC reserves a small amount of memory for hardware components. It only becomes a concern when several gigabytes are unavailable without an obvious reason.

mainEntity.name: Can I disable hardware reserved memory?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't completely disable it because some hardware requires reserved memory to function. However, if an unusually large amount is reserved due to a configuration issue, correcting the underlying problem can make that memory available again.

mainEntity.name: Does upgrading RAM fix this?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you're genuinely running out of memory. If Windows is reserving large portions of your installed RAM because of BIOS or configuration issues, installing additional memory won't help much. It's better to identify why the existing memory isn't fully usable first.

mainEntity.name: Does predictive text work offline?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Once enabled, Text Suggestions and Autocorrect work without an internet connection because they're built into Windows 11.

mainEntity.name: Why don't text suggestions appear?

acceptedAnswer.text: There are several possible reasons. Text suggestions isn't enabled in Settings > Time & Language > Typing, or the application you're using may not support Windows' predictive typing. Also, the feature is not available in all languages.

acceptedAnswer.text: If your system is completely frozen and you can't even access the menus, then do a hard restart of the console itself by pressing and holding the power button for at least 15 seconds. This method works more or less the same way across all three consoles.

title.rendered: Meta introduces Muse Image, its first Superintelligence Labs AI generator

content.rendered:
Meta has launched Muse Image, its first image generation model developed by Meta Superintelligence Labs. The new model is rolling out inside the Meta AI app and will also power creative features across Instagram and WhatsApp.

The launch follows Meta’s shift earlier this year from its Llama AI models to Muse Spark, the company’s newer AI system behind its latest Meta AI features.

Generate images with text prompts

Muse Image works like other AI image generators, allowing users to create images by entering a text description. The tool uses Muse Spark’s reasoning capabilities to better understand prompts, use additional context from the web when needed, and generate more accurate images.

Since Muse Image is integrated with Meta’s apps, it can also use uploaded photos, tagged friend profiles, and trending information from platforms like Facebook to create more personalized results.

Users can download generated images and share them directly to their feeds, stories, or chats.

1/ releasing muse image today — the first image generation model from MSL. it's agentic: pairs with muse spark to reason through your prompt, search the web, and plan before it generates. people get what they meant on the first try. live now in the Meta AI app. pic.twitter.com/7KUk0DS1as

— Alexandr Wang (@alexandr_wang) July 7, 2026

New AI tools coming to Meta apps

Meta says Muse Image is already powering new creative features across its apps. Instagram users are getting access to more than 30 new AI-powered effects for Stories, while WhatsApp users in select countries can generate images directly inside chats with Meta AI.

The company plans to expand Muse Image to more countries and additional apps, including Facebook and Messenger. More areas of Instagram and WhatsApp will also gain support in future updates.

Meta also plans to bring Muse Image to advertisers and agencies through Advantage+ creative, allowing businesses to use the model for AI-generated advertising content.

The company confirmed that Muse Video is already in development, suggesting video generation will be the next major addition to Meta’s AI tools after Muse Spark and Muse Image.

Would you use Muse Image instead of other AI image generators? Let us know in the comments below.
